# fp tracker snapshot

**Generated by `data-raw/snapshot-tracker.sh` on 2026-08-07.**
286 issues. Do not hand-edit: the next run overwrites this file
wholesale.

`.fp/` is gitignored, so this file is the only copy of the tracker in
git. It is a backstop for the SITE-* citations in
`docs/architecture.md` and the other docs under `docs/`, not a replacement for the tracker: `fp` remains
authoritative and `fp context <id>` remains the way to read an issue.

## SITE-agfcwgmh: E.1a: page-fetch artifact + acquisition (Contract A, engine-neutral)

**Status:** done | **Parent:** ihycidflmgtcvnctecfqldgdulicucex

### Description

### E.1a: page-fetch artifact + acquisition (Contract A, engine-neutral)

Governing: `docs/design/layer-e-page-inspection.md` §0.1, §3.1, §3.2. **Engine identity MUST NOT leak into the fetch** — this is server+URL mechanics.

#### The artifact
Internal `page_fetch_artifact` (NOT added to the pinned `source_metadata()` columns):
- `requested_url`, `final_url`
- `hops`: ordered, one record per HTTP request (`url`, `status`, resolved `Location`) — a redirect chain is representable
- `terminal_headers`: final response headers, **preserving repeated fields** (multiple `X-Robots-Tag` / `Link`)
- `body`: retained prefix capped at the per-page cap + `truncated` flag (truncate-and-retain)
- `outcome`: ADR-009 §2 `evidence_status` incl. the amended `partial` (per the page-inspection ADR)
- `request_user_agent`: the HTTP header actually sent — recorded for the "what did the inspector see" caveat; **distinct** from any engine product token

#### Safety precedence (§0.5)
- SSRF / scheme / downgrade → `safety_refused` (→ `PAGE_SSRF_BLOCKED` at E.1f).
- Per-page cap reached → `partial`, prefix retained.
- 500 MB ceiling → discard backstop → resource failure (→ `PAGE_FETCH_FAILED` at E.1f), **not** SSRF.

#### Also
- **Content-type via byte sniffing**, not blind trust of the `Content-Type` header (a mislabeled body must not corrupt extraction status).
- Fetches an **unrendered** snapshot (no JS) — stamp this so downstream absence findings carry the caveat.

#### Depends on
The page-inspection ADR (`partial`, safety/resource precedence).

#### Blocks
E.1s, E.1f, and (via E.1f) E.2/E.3/E.4.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-19 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Done — PR #158 squash-merged to main. Internal page_fetch_artifact + page_fetch() acquisition (engine-neutral Contract A) over the ADR-003 machinery; fetch_source() frozen byte-identical; 61 mocked tests; gate green. Downgrade-rejection deferred → SITE-iqqoekjk (close before/with E.1f).

## SITE-ahhxlnfn: fixture-plan.md 2.7 names three encoding fixtures that do not exist

**Status:** done | **Parent:** nlptpmdqqvmldzbdrfwhwlceepjoksne

### Description

### Defect

docs/fixture-plan.md SS2.7 'Encoding scenarios' lists three fixtures by name:

| Scenario | Fixture | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| BOM-prefixed UTF-8 | encoding-bom-utf8.xml | Passes |
| BOM vs XML declaration conflict | encoding-bom-vs-decl.xml | Strict warning |
| HTTP charset vs BOM conflict | encoding-charset-conflict.xml | ENCODING_CONFLICT info |

None of the three exists. `find tests -name 'encoding-*'` returns nothing. The actual corpus (tests/testthat/fixtures/corpus/encoding/, imported under SITE-uivyzfhe) holds six differently-named files: bom-conflict.xml, declared-iso8859-no-bom.xml, declared-utf8-no-bom.xml, no-encoding.xml, utf16-le-bom.xml, utf8-bom.xml.

Verified 2026-07-29 at e35fc57.

### The substantive half

Two rows map cleanly onto imported fixtures (encoding-bom-utf8 -> utf8-bom.xml, encoding-bom-vs-decl -> bom-conflict.xml, both now behaving as the plan says after SITE-vepzywnc). The third does not, and cannot:

**`encoding-charset-conflict.xml` is unbuildable as a corpus fixture.** The corpus harness drives every file through `validate_sitemap(path)` on a LOCAL path, and a local file has no HTTP response -- so http_charset is always NA and the HTTP-charset leg of ENCODING_CONFLICT can never fire from the corpus. That leg is covered instead by a mocked-response test (test-encoding-facts.R). So the plan row describes a scenario the corpus format cannot express.

### Fix

Rename the three rows to the fixtures that actually exist and record their real expected outcomes, and either drop the charset row or annotate it as mock-only, not corpus-only. Related in kind to SITE-fbngvttn (findings-contract.md prose contradicting the shipped registry).

## SITE-anmruolj: Expose request customization for headers, authentication, and proxies

**Status:** done | **Parent:** oauvnvtcipfjvkzrbfdawnunuowjwnvx

### Description

What: Add a supported public way to mutate or configure httr2 requests for custom headers, authentication, cookies, proxy settings, and TLS options.

Why: Real sitemap sources may sit behind staging authentication, CDN bot controls, corporate proxies, or custom TLS requirements. user_agent alone is insufficient.

## SITE-aojjbdhq: Text path does not strip the UTF-8 BOM, corrupting the first URL

**Status:** done | **Parent:** nlptpmdqqvmldzbdrfwhwlceepjoksne

### Description

### Claim

The text-sitemap path does not strip the UTF-8 BOM, silently corrupting the first URL.

`text_as_string()` does `rawToChar()` + `Encoding<-"UTF-8"` (`R/parse-text.R:22-29`) and `parse_sitemap_text()` only `trimws()`es each line (`:45-56`). U+FEFF is **not** POSIX whitespace, so it survives `trimws()` and remains prepended to the first `<loc>`.

The comparison reports running this: a BOM followed by `http` yields `nchar == 5` rather than 4 — i.e. the BOM is still there.

`sitemap-validator` strips it before decoding (`src/lib/services/pipeline/pipeline.ts:463`).

### Step 1 — Verify before coding (REQUIRED)

Reproduce directly in an R session — this one is cheap and unambiguous:

```r
x <- as.raw(c(0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF, 0x68, 0x74, 0x74, 0x70))
s <- rawToChar(x); Encoding(s) <- "UTF-8"
nchar(trimws(s))   # expect 5 if the BOM survives, 4 if stripped
```

Then confirm end to end: a BOM-prefixed text sitemap whose first line is a valid URL — does that URL come back intact, and does a spurious finding fire on it?

Check the XML path separately; the claim is specific to text.

### Why it matters

Silent data corruption on the first URL of every BOM-prefixed text sitemap. BOMs are common in files produced on Windows, and the failure is invisible — the URL is simply wrong, and any `<loc>` rule that fires on it reports a misleading value.

### Approach

Strip a leading UTF-8 BOM in `text_as_string()`, on the raw bytes before `rawToChar()`. Handle UTF-16 BOMs too, or reject them explicitly — do not leave them to `rawToChar()`.

### Files

- `R/parse-text.R` — `text_as_string()`
- `tests/testthat/` — BOM-prefixed text fixture

### Done

A BOM-prefixed text sitemap yields the correct first URL; UTF-16 BOMs are handled or explicitly rejected; the corpus text fixtures agree with the sibling.


### Comments

#### 2026-07-28 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

VERIFIED — CONFIRMED (2026-07-29).

Step 1 snippet reproduces exactly as predicted: nchar(trimws(s)) == 5, not 4.

End-to-end through parse_sitemap_text() on a BOM-prefixed 2-line text sitemap:
- loc[1] nchar = 22 vs 21 for the clean URL
- utf8ToInt(substr(loc[1],1,3)) = 65279,104,116 — U+FEFF is the leading codepoint of the first loc

So the first URL of every BOM-prefixed text sitemap is silently corrupted. Confirmed at R/parse-text.R:22-29 (text_as_string does rawToChar + Encoding<- with no BOM strip) and :48 (trimws does not touch U+FEFF).

Proceeding to fix: strip the BOM on the raw bytes before rawToChar().

#### 2026-07-28 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

DONE — committed 2583b48 on chore/site-nlptpmdq-crossport-verify.

The BOM strip in text_as_string() alone was NOT sufficient. Three call sites decoded text bytes independently and only one went through the parser helper:

1. R/validate-sitemap.R:809 — bare rawToChar(src$bytes). This was the actual production defect for validation: validate_sitemap() on a BOM-prefixed text file emitted a spurious PROTOCOL_URL_NOT_ABSOLUTE, because the BOM arrived as a *character* and text_as_string() took its non-raw branch, which never strips.
2. R/audit-pipeline.R:397 — same bare rawToChar. Caught by the audit-vs-validate equality cross-check at test-audit-pipeline.R:120, which started failing once (1) was fixed. That test earned its keep.
3. R/probe.R probe_text_url_count() — documents that it mirrors parse_sitemap_text(), so it moved too to keep the stated invariant true. Behavior delta is confined to a BOM-only document, which now counts 0 URL lines instead of 1.

Also handled the UTF-16/UTF-32 BOM case the issue asked about: rejected explicitly with sitemapr_text_parse_error rather than left to fail inside rawToChar().

NOTABLE: tests/testthat/fixtures/corpus-golden.tsv had text/utf8-bom.txt -> PROTOCOL_URL_NOT_ABSOLUTE recorded as the EXPECTED outcome. The fixture is three valid absolute URLs, so the golden had enshrined the bug. Regenerated via REGEN_CORPUS_GOLDEN=1; exactly one line changes, to <none>. Flagging for SITE-ppojfsed: corpus-golden.tsv is named there as the cross-port join baseline, and it was carrying at least one wrong expectation. Worth asking whether the sibling agrees (also buggy) or diverges (in which case the golden was never genuinely cross-checked).

Gate: full suite 0 failures, lint clean, coverage 100.00% on all four touched files.

## SITE-arkarkop: S10: Source-context preset constructors (gsc_submission/robots_cross_submission) (§12.1/§12.2c ergonomics)

**Status:** done | **Parent:** mnahrdntglketxnrybimlrqxnseyjvha

### Description

What: Add construction-time preset constructors that bundle the four independent per-source context axes into a coherent 'declare the source once' context, so a user can express e.g. a GSC submission without hand-setting three axes.

Why: The four ruleset_context() axes (submission_channel / authority_evidence / property_scope / discovery_provenance) are deliberately independent for REPRESENTABILITY (divergent + 'conflicting' states must stay expressible). But the common case ('this was a GSC submission for property X, so cross-domain should validate') is currently low-level: a user must set submission_channel=search_console_api AND authority_evidence=verified_property_set AND property_scope by hand (S5). A construction-time preset gives the ergonomic 'batch toggle' the design originally envisioned WITHOUT bending the independence principle: the preset just returns a normal ruleset_context() with a coherent bundle; the (c) evaluator (loc_authority_established/loc_authority_covers) is UNCHANGED, and every axis stays independently overridable. Decided against evaluation-time coupling (treating search_console_api as itself sufficient authority) because it forces an invented precedence rule when the channel implies authority but authority_evidence says 'conflicting'.

How:
- Add gsc_submission(property) -> ruleset_context(submission_channel='search_console_api', authority_evidence='verified_property_set', property_scope=property). property is the irreducible input (which verified property/host); it cannot be inferred.
- Add robots_cross_submission() sibling for the target-host robots.txt reference case -> ruleset_context(authority_evidence='target_host_robots_reference') (discovery_provenance='robots_txt_reference' as the discovery sense may also be set; keep authority = the trust sense).
- @export both; roxygen with @seealso ruleset_context(); regenerate NAMESPACE+man (roxygen2 8.0.0) and commit.
- Do NOT change the (c) evaluator or any validity rule; this is context-layer ergonomics only. Baseline byte-identical (presets only produce contexts consumed by the engine-aware surface).

Files: R/ruleset-context.R; tests/testthat/test-ruleset-context.R; NAMESPACE+man/*.Rd (generated); maybe a docs mention.

Done: gsc_submission()/robots_cross_submission() return correct ruleset_context() bundles; a validate_sitemap_ruleset(src,'google',context=gsc_submission('https://other.com/')) accepts a cross-host <loc> on that property; axes remain independently overridable; exports documented + roxygen clean fixpoint. Sequencing: RUN LAST, after S9. Deps: S5 (done).

## SITE-babrgssv: Add a recommendations section to report_sitemap()

**Status:** done | **Parent:** nlptpmdqqvmldzbdrfwhwlceepjoksne

### Description

### Claim

`report_sitemap()` has no equivalent of the sibling's **recommendations section** (`src/lib/report-html/index.ts:822-887`) — prescriptive guidance with primary-source citations rather than raw findings. It covers stale-`lastmod` detection at a 50% threshold, `priority`/`changefreq` presence, URL count against 50,000, index count against 500, and children per index against 1,000, each citing the source (Bing lastmod blog, Google's large-sitemaps and 2008 index guidance).

Every input it needs reportedly already exists in sitemapr's `urls` / `tree` / `findings` tibbles.

### Step 1 — Verify before coding (REQUIRED)

1. Confirm no recommendations equivalent exists in `R/report.R`.
2. Confirm the inputs are available without new computation — lastmod distribution is already computed for `report_lastmod_section()` (`R/report.R:369`), and index/child counts for `report_sitemap_table()` (`:258`).
3. **Check each citation against `docs/sitemap-spec.md` §12 and `docs/references.md` before reusing it.** §12.6 records that Bing's 2008 10 MB and 2009 XML-only statements must *not* enter the `bing` ruleset as current policy, and §12.4 records the anonymous ping as deprecated (`advisory`). The sibling's citations were written before that analysis and may assert as current something §12 classifies as historical. Do not port a citation you have not re-checked.

### Why it matters

Moves the report from diagnostic to prescriptive. The thresholds are already known to sitemapr; only the framing is missing.

### Approach

Render after the findings block. Keep each recommendation traceable to a source, and tag provenance consistently with the ADR-009 §0 vocabulary where a recommendation rests on an engine's documented behaviour rather than the protocol — `advisory` for tool-observed, `documented` for current official guidance, and nothing at all for statements §12 marks superseded.

### Files

- `R/report.R`
- `docs/references.md` — citation sources

### Done

Reports carry a recommendations section; every citation is verified current against §12; recommendations resting on engine behaviour carry the right provenance tag.


### Comments

Step 2 CONFIRMED: every input is already in hand. urls$lastmod is POSIXct/UTC (report_lastmod_section() already computes the coverage split), urls$priority (numeric) and urls$changefreq (character) are columns, and per-source byte size + format + per-source URL counts are already derived by report_sitemap_table() from attr(urls, 'sources'). No new computation and no new fetch.

Step 3 — CITATION AUDIT, and the issue's warning was justified. Two of the sibling's five thresholds must NOT be ported as stated:
- 'index count against 500' is NOT a file rule. sitemap-spec.md §12.6 classifies 500 sitemap-index files as a Google Search Console SUBMISSION/property cap (docs/references.md line 29, Google large-sitemaps). It may only be rendered as a submission-scope note, ruleset=google, provenance documented.
- 'children per index against 1,000' is WRONG in every current source. §12.6: child sitemaps per index = 50,000 for baseline/google/bing/yandex. 1,000 appears to descend from the 2008 Google index guidance, which §12.6's source-precedence rule excludes from a current cell.
Also pinned by §12.6: the size bound is 50 MB = 52,428,800 bytes (binary MiB), not 50,000,000 — sitemapr is already correct here (R/protocol-validate.R:250) and the recommendation must use the same figure.
Citations that survive as current: sitemaps.org protocol (50,000 URLs / 50 MB / 50,000 index children, inherited_protocol); Google build-sitemap ('Google ignores changefreq/priority', lastmod only if verifiably accurate, documented); Bing Feb-2023 lastmod-importance post (lastmod disregarded when dishonest, documented) and Bing Jul-2025 post (key recrawl signal, date+time; ignores changefreq/priority, documented). NOT cited: Bing 2008 10 MB and 2009 XML-only (§12.6 historical), and the deprecated anonymous ping (§12.4).
The 50% staleness threshold and the 'approaching the cap' fraction are sitemapr's own product decisions, so they carry application_choice per ADR-009 §0, not documented.

copy of rurl).

by design, so no file may be added unilaterally. Each want below is currently

pinned but the CROSS-PORT AGREEMENT is not — the golden join has no row.

### The seven wants

1. **Text duplicates** — `PROTOCOL_DUPLICATE_LOC` on a byte-identical repeat
   (SITE-lcmvzpel). No text fixture contains a duplicate URL.
2. **Text count cap** — needs a parameterizable `max_url_count`.
3. **Unparseable priority** (SITE-prnqukft).
4. **Binary input.**
5. **A real UTF-16 document** (SITE-zarjabyz) — declaration + UTF-16LE BOM +
   an actually UTF-16LE body. `encoding/utf16-le-bom.xml` is NOT one: it is a
   UTF-16LE BOM on an ASCII body declaring UTF-8 (170 bytes, hexdump-verified),
   genuinely malformed, and its golden line is correct as-is.
6. **Decompression bomb** (SITE-vsjtaejc). Wrinkle: a useful fixture is by
   nature a huge-expansion blob, awkward against the 5 MB
   `check-added-large-files` hook, so it may need to be GENERATED at test time
   from a documented recipe — a first for this corpus, needing sibling
   agreement. Recipe: `gzfile()` + `writeBin(raw(n))`, NOT
   `memCompress(type="gzip")` (that emits a bare zlib stream `78 9c` which the
   sniffer classifies binary, so it never reaches the gzip path).
7. **Aggregate traversal budgets** (SITE-ppojfsed, e36571b) —
   `INDEX_TOTAL_SITEMAPS_EXCEEDED` / `INDEX_TOTAL_URLS_EXCEEDED` have zero
   corpus rows and cannot get one: the budgets default to `Inf` and the corpus
   runner passes no override. Their severity and subject_type just changed on
   the sitemapr side with the golden provably unmoved.

### The structural finding underneath (the reason to fix the harness, not add files)

`test-corpus-fixtures.R` drives every fixture through `validate_sitemap(path)`
as a **local file**. A local file has no response, so `charset` and
`content_type` are always `NA`.

**Anything keyed off response headers is outside the golden corpus by
construction** — Content-Type, charset, Content-Encoding, and the whole
classification-by-declared-type surface. That is not a missing fixture; no
fixture can express it. Wants 2, 6 and 7 are the same shape (they need a
parameter, not a file).

So the harness needs two capabilities before more fixtures are worth adding:
per-case **limit/option overrides**, and per-case **response metadata**.

### Also worth auditing first

From SITE-vepzywnc: the six `encoding/` fixtures are byte-identical to the
sibling's but the sibling ships NO TEST referencing any of them — grepping its
`src/` and `tests/` for the filenames returns nothing. A shared fixture with a
golden on one side only is **not a join row**. Audit how many of the ~79
imported fixtures are in that state before designing the harness around them;
it may be most of them.

And `corpus-golden.tsv` has been WRONG twice where nobody was cross-checking
(`text/utf8-bom.txt` enshrined the BOM bug; `encoding/bom-conflict.xml` sat at
`<none>` because the producer did not exist). A golden only ever regenerated
from the implementation it tests cannot catch that class of error — the
sibling side has to be independently recorded.

### Done

Harness supports per-case option overrides and response metadata; the
one-sided-fixture audit is recorded; each of the seven wants is either a shared
corpus row agreed with the sibling or explicitly recorded as out of scope with
a reason.

### Files

- `tests/testthat/test-corpus-fixtures.R`
- `tests/testthat/fixtures/corpus-golden.tsv` (regenerable; outside the
  byte-identical directory)
- Sibling: `~/Projects/sitemap-validator/fixtures/`

### Comments

#### 2026-07-30 — bartek@turczynski.pl

DONE at d8cd5d2. Verify gate green.

AUDIT FIRST (the issue said to do this before designing around the fixtures) — and it changed two conclusions:

1. The byte-identity claim in test-corpus-fixtures.R and fixtures/COPYRIGHTS is FALSE. Checked by checksum myself rather than trusting a report: 79/80 paths shared, 78 of those identical, THREE divergences, all from sitemapr's side.
     xml/unsupported-root.xml                 content differs — sitemapr rewrote it <rss> -> <catalog> at 8d5bf83 when feeds became parseable; sibling still ships the <rss>. That golden row compares two different documents, which is worse than having no row.
     xml/video-no-player-or-content-loc.xml   sitemapr only, added at 64e4119 (SITE-ciedgveo)
     xml/valid-pagemap.xml                    sibling only, never imported
   Both unilateral changes were made despite the standing rule, and were invisible precisely because the harness kept ASSERTING identity in prose while nothing checked it. Filed cross-repo as SMV-swnyfhjr. Both file headers now state the real state.

2. SITE-vepzywnc's premise is REFUTED, so do not design around it. It suspected the six encoding/ fixtures are referenced by no sibling test. In fact 79 of 80 fixtures are referenced there — all via fixtures/index.ts, many also by fixtures.test.ts and the e2e suites. The ONLY unreferenced file is sitemapr's own unilateral addition. So the corpus is not mostly one-sided; it is 78/80 genuinely shared.

The real structural gap is different from 'one-sided fixtures': the sibling has NO golden table at all (hand-written assertions in a 525-line fixtures.test.ts). corpus-golden.tsv is therefore only ever regenerated from sitemapr's own implementation and cannot catch code+golden being wrong together — which is exactly how text/utf8-bom.txt and encoding/bom-conflict.xml went wrong. Recording the sibling side as a joinable table is the larger half of SMV-swnyfhjr; this issue does not claim to have done it, and the harness header says so rather than implying otherwise.

HARNESS: added a parameterized-case layer — same fixture bytes plus per-case options, validate_sitemap() args, and optionally a SERVED response (httr2 mock). Pinned in its own corpus-cases-golden.tsv, deliberately NOT folded into corpus-golden.tsv: the latter is the cross-port artifact where every row claims something about both ports, and the sibling has no notion of these parameters. Folding them in would claim an agreement nobody checked.

THE SEVEN WANTS (recorded in fixture-plan.md §3.2a):
  1 text duplicates          OUT — needs shared fixture content; pinned in test-protocol-validate.R
  2 text count cap           CASE ROW — text/valid.txt max_url_count=1
  3 unparseable priority     OUT — priority-out-of-range.xml is out-of-range, not unparseable
  4 binary input             OUT — no corpus file is a binary blob
  5 real UTF-16 document     OUT — built in test-encoding-facts.R; utf16-le-bom.xml's golden is correct as-is
  6 decompression bomb       CASE ROWS — no blob and no generated-fixture convention needed. Lowering the inflated-size ceiling over the real 280-byte compressed/valid.xml.gz reaches the same guard. The .tar.gz ceiling is a second case and behaves DIFFERENTLY (raises sitemapr_archive_limit rather than reporting a finding), which is worth having pinned.
  7 aggregate budgets        CASE ROWS — and the issue's diagnosis was incomplete: the blocker is not only that the runner passes no override. A local index is NEVER TRAVERSED (children are remote URLs), so these cannot trip from a file at ANY limit. Verified, not assumed. They need the response layer, not just the option layer.

Two harness details that earned themselves immediately:
  * A case must CHANGE the plain-file outcome, asserted. An agreeing-response-charset case produced no finding — it could never fail — so the guard rejected it and it was dropped instead of committed.
  * The served URL is on example.com, the host the fixtures' own URLs use. A different host made every served case additionally report PROTOCOL_URL_OUT_OF_SCOPE: noise the harness itself created.

## SITE-cdfeqvwq: F.5 Feed detection: sniff_format recognizes RSS/Atom; validate_sitemap emits UNSUPPORTED_FEED for index feed-children

**Status:** done | **Parent:** ymzvnlprytjfrnfgfrozeujxsndbsfpd

### Description

**Layer F slice — unit F.5 (feed detection). Resolves the design-fork found during F.2 (PR #34): no machinery surfaces a 'this child is a feed' signal, so the index feed-child -> UNSUPPORTED_FEED path is currently inert.** Depends on F.2 (merged). BLOCKS F.4 (SITE-vidksshc) — its index-rss-child.xml scenario needs UNSUPPORTED_FEED.

### The gap
- sniff_format() (R/sniff.R) returns generic 'xml' for an <rss>/<feed> root — no feed verdict.
- expand_index() records each fetched child in its returned `sources` with the sniffed `format`; a feed child currently sniffs as 'xml' and parse_dispatch errors on it -> a harmless category='classification' 'could not be parsed; skipped' problem (NOT surfaced as a finding).
- The OUTPUT path already exists (D.6): source_meta(feed_children = <urls>) -> validate_classification() emits one UNSUPPORTED_FEED per child ('Sitemap-index child <url> is an RSS/Atom feed...'). Only DETECTION is missing.

### Edits (scope = EXACTLY these files)
#### Edit 1 — R/sniff.R
sniff_format(): after the urlset and sitemapindex root checks and BEFORE the HTML and generic-xml catch-alls, recognize RSS and Atom roots and return 'feed':
- RSS: `^<rss([[:space:]>/]|$)` (optional ns prefix allowed, mirror the existing urlset/sitemapindex regexes: `^<([a-z0-9_.-]+:)?rss(...)`).
- Atom: `^<([a-z0-9_.-]+:)?feed([[:space:]>/]|$)`.
Placement matters: a sitemap urlset/sitemapindex must NEVER be mis-sniffed as a feed (those checks already run first). Update the function's documented return-value set / any header listing formats to include 'feed'.

#### Edit 2 — R/validate-sitemap.R
Replace the inert `index_feed_children()` (which greps problem messages for 'feed') with detection off the expansion `sources`: in validate_index_parts(), after expand_index(), collect the final_url of every `ex$sources` record whose `format == 'feed'`, and if any, add `validate_classification(source_meta(feed_children = <those urls>), src$base)` to parts. Remove the old problem-message-grep helper. (The feed child's 'could not be parsed' problem in ex$problems is harmless — index_problem_code() only maps category=='index-expansion', so it is never turned into a finding; leave it.)
Top-level feed source (src$format == 'feed' at the entrypoint, no index): OUT OF SCOPE for v1 — let the existing XML branch handle it (an <rss> root is not a sitemap root, so it yields UNSUPPORTED_ROOT). No active scenario requires UNSUPPORTED_FEED for a top-level feed; do not extend the classification message contract for it. Add a one-line comment noting this.

### Tests
- tests/testthat/test-sniff.R: add cases — `<rss version=...>` -> 'feed'; an Atom `<feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom">` -> 'feed'; and a regression assert that a urlset and a sitemapindex still sniff as xml-urlset / xml-sitemapindex (not 'feed').
- tests/testthat/test-validate-sitemap.R: add an OFFLINE case (httr2::local_mocked_responses, following the existing index/url pattern in this file) — a sitemapindex whose child <loc> returns RSS bytes -> validate_sitemap() produces an UNSUPPORTED_FEED finding (severity info or warning), full 10-column contract. Do NOT rely on the F.4 cucumber fixture; build the mocked index+child inline or with a tiny local fixture.

### Acceptance
- sniff_format() returns 'feed' for RSS and Atom roots; urlset/sitemapindex unaffected.
- validate_sitemap() over a sitemapindex with an RSS/Atom feed child produces UNSUPPORTED_FEED via the existing source_meta/classification path.
- Verify gate passes (0E/0W/1NOTE pre-existing).

### Verify gate
Rscript -e 'lints <- lintr::lint_package(); if (length(lints)) { print(lints); quit(status = 1) }; rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = "--as-cran", error_on = "warning")'

### Dependencies
F.2 (merged). Blocks F.4.

### Comments

#### 2026-06-28 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

SCOPE ADDITION (orchestrator, fork resolved Option A): F.5 also fixes the DOCTYPE-internal-subset sniffer bug, alongside feed detection — both are sniff_format changes.

#### Edit 3 (added) — R/sniff.R sniff_strip_prologue()
A DOCTYPE with an internal subset, e.g. `<!DOCTYPE urlset [ <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "..."> ]>`, currently stops the DOCTYPE-strip at the FIRST '>' (the end of the ENTITY line), leaving ']>...<urlset>' so the root isn't found and the doc falls through to the TEXT classifier (misrouting XML sitemaps to the text producer; defeats the XXE cucumber scenario). Fix: when stripping a DOCTYPE that contains an internal subset, skip from '[' to the matching ']' and then to the following '>'. Keep the existing no-internal-subset DOCTYPE path working (e.g. '<!DOCTYPE html>'). Add the bracket-skip carefully — the internal subset can itself contain '>' chars inside ENTITY/ELEMENT declarations.

#### Tests (added)
- test-sniff.R: a urlset behind a DOCTYPE-with-internal-subset (the xxe-attempt.xml shape) now sniffs as xml-urlset (NOT text); '<!DOCTYPE html>' still -> html; a plain urlset still -> xml-urlset.
- This makes validate_sitemap() route xxe-attempt.xml through the XML schema/protocol path; the F.3 XXE cucumber step will be corrected (separately, on the F.3 branch) to assert the XML-path truth (entity expands to empty / SCHEMA_INVALID 'entity references'), so do NOT touch the cucumber files in F.5.

Acceptance addition: xxe-attempt.xml (and any DOCTYPE+internal-subset urlset) sniffs as xml-urlset; existing sniff tests stay green.

## SITE-ciedgveo: video: the one-of(player_loc, content_loc) rule is enforced nowhere

**Status:** done | **Parent:** nlptpmdqqvmldzbdrfwhwlceepjoksne

### Description

### Claim

The Sitemap Protocol's video rule "at least one of `<video:player_loc>` or `<video:content_loc>` must be present" is **enforced nowhere in sitemapr** — it falls through the crack between two layers, each of which believes the other owns it.

- The protocol layer defers to schema: comment at `R/protocol-validate.R:671-672` says the rule is "left to the schema layer".
- The schema says it cannot express it: `inst/schemas/sitemap-video.xsd:17` — *"the protocol's 'at least one of player_loc / content_loc' rule cannot be expressed…"* — and both elements are `minOccurs="0"` (`:98`, `:107`).

Grepping `content_loc|player_loc` across `R/` reportedly returns **only that comment**.

`sitemap-validator` enforces it at layer D (`src/lib/services/protocol/fields.ts:351-364`).

### Step 1 — Verify before coding (REQUIRED)

1. `grep -rn "content_loc\|player_loc" R/ inst/` — confirm no enforcement.
2. Construct a `<video:video>` entry with neither element and run `validate_sitemap()` in strict mode. Confirm nothing fires. **This is the decisive check** — the grep could miss an indirect path.
3. Confirm which finding code should carry it: `PROTOCOL_VIDEO_FIELD_INVALID` already exists in `docs/findings-registry.csv`, and the sibling uses it. Reuse rather than mint.

### Why it matters

This is the best find in the whole comparison: a genuine, unambiguous spec rule that neither layer enforces because each documented the other as owner. It is exactly the class of defect a cross-port comparison exists to catch.

### Approach

Enforce in the protocol layer alongside the other video field rules, using the existing code. Correct the misleading comment at `R/protocol-validate.R:671-672` and the XSD comment so the ownership question cannot recur.

### Files

- `R/protocol-validate.R` — video extension validation
- `inst/schemas/sitemap-video.xsd` — comment only
- `tests/testthat/test-protocol-validate.R`

### Done

A `<video:video>` with neither `player_loc` nor `content_loc` emits `PROTOCOL_VIDEO_FIELD_INVALID`; both comments name the real owner; the sibling and sitemapr agree on the fixture.


### Comments

#### 2026-07-28 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

VERIFIED — CONFIRMED (2026-07-29), and isolated with controls.

A <video:video> carrying thumbnail_loc + title + description but NEITHER player_loc NOR content_loc produces ZERO findings — not a protocol finding, not SCHEMA_INVALID.

Two controls prove the video path is otherwise live on the same fixture shape:
- <video:duration>999999</video:duration> -> SCHEMA_INVALID + PROTOCOL_VIDEO_FIELD_INVALID
- omitting the required <video:title> -> SCHEMA_INVALID

So the extension IS parsed and IS validated at both layers; only the one-of rule falls through the gap. The comment at R/protocol-validate.R:671-672 ("required-child presence and the content_loc/player_loc one-of rule are structural and left to the schema layer") is the misdirection — the XSD enforces required-child presence but not the one-of.

Confirms the epic framing: this is the best find in the comparison. Proceeding to enforce in the protocol layer and correct both comments.

#### 2026-07-28 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

DONE — committed 64e4119 on chore/site-nlptpmdq-crossport-verify.

Ownership resolved in favor of the protocol layer, and the reason is not arbitrary: the alternation genuinely cannot be expressed in XSD 1.0 (each element must be individually optional there), so the protocol layer is the ONLY place it can be caught. The XSD comment at inst/schemas/sitemap-video.xsd:17-19 already said exactly this and was correct all along; the misdirection was one-sided, at R/protocol-validate.R:669-672 ("structural and left to the schema layer"). Corrected that comment to state why the rule lives here, so the question cannot recur.

docs/sitemap-spec.md §5.3 also already documented both the rule and PROTOCOL_VIDEO_FIELD_INVALID as its code — so the spec and the schema were both right, and only the implementation and one code comment were missing. Nothing to change in the docs.

Implemented as video_one_of_loc_msgs() inside validate_video_element(), reusing PROTOCOL_VIDEO_FIELD_INVALID — no new registry code, as the issue directed. False-positive check: player_loc alone, content_loc alone, and both present are all clean; only "neither" fires. ## SITE-cklgdzwq: 13 files are drifted from the pre-commit hooks' own formatting

**Status:** done

### Description

### Claim

Thirteen tracked files are not in the state this project's own pre-commit hooks produce. Running the pre-push stage rewrites them:

**`air-format` reformats R sources** (one-argument-per-line style):
- `R/url.R`, `R/discovery.R`, `R/decompression-validate.R`
- `tests/testthat/test-discovery-engine.R`, `test-read-sitemap.R`, `test-schema-profile.R`, `test-url.R`

**`end-of-file-fixer` strips a trailing blank line**:
- `.editorconfig`, `.env.example`, `.gitattributes`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `inst/schemas/LICENSE`, `inst/schemas/SOURCES.md`

Applying air's reformat then **fails lintr**: collapsing an argument list in `tests/testthat/test-discovery-engine.R:189` produces an 89-character line, over the 80-char `line_length_linter` limit. So the drift cannot simply be committed as-is — the reformat and the lint fix have to land together.

### Why it went unnoticed

Per-commit hooks run on **staged files only**, so a commit that does not touch these files never reformats them. The `verify` hook is `always_run: true` at the **pre-push** stage, which is the only thing that sees the whole tree — and every push has 403ed since the GitHub account suspension (2026-07-28), so the gate has not executed since. Discovered 2026-07-29 by pushing to a local bare mirror, which fired the hooks for the first time in two days.

### Why it matters

The tree does not satisfy its own gate. Whoever pushes first after the suspension lifts gets 13 unrelated files in their diff plus a lint failure that has nothing to do with their change — and the natural reaction (committing the hook output) ships a lint-failing tree.

### Approach

One dedicated commit, nothing else in it. Run the pre-push hooks over the whole tree, fix the resulting long line in `test-discovery-engine.R`, then run the full verify chain plus coverage before committing. The R/ files are real source changes even though they are formatting-only, so they need the same verification as any other change.

Worth checking while in there whether `air.toml` and `.lintr` agree on line width — a formatter that can produce a line the linter rejects is a standing trap, not a one-off.

### Files

- the 13 listed above
- `air.toml`, `.lintr` (consistency check)

### Done

`pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage pre-push` leaves the tree unmodified and exits clean; full verify chain green; coverage unchanged at 100%.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-30 — bartek@turczynski.pl

DONE in f1afbf8 (branch chore/site-nlptpmdq-crossport-verify).

### Claim verified in full, by execution

All 13 files confirmed drifted before editing: the pinned 0.8.2 air-format hook rewrote exactly the 7 R/test files listed, and all 6 EOF files carried a trailing blank line (last two bytes 0a0a). The predicted lint failure was exact -- collapsing the body_map argument list in test-discovery-engine.R:189 produces an 89-character line, the only lint in the package.

### The version-mismatch worry does not apply

SITE-dxujycqe argued the real root cause was local air 0.10.0 vs the hook-pinned 0.8.2, and that running air by hand starts a rewrite war. Not true on this tree: I captured both patches and diffed them -- byte-identical, 135 lines each. Either version produces the same result, so the mismatch is currently inert. Worth re-testing rather than assuming, if air is bumped again.

### One defect neither issue recorded

air relocates an end-of-line comment after an opening brace onto its own line. That silently detached the # nolint from decompression_findings_from_problems, a 36-character name that object_length_linter flags. The linter is a lintr *default*, so it is absent from .lintr (which uses defaults = list()) and absent from goodpractice 60-linter set, but live for anything running lintr defaults -- which is presumably why fddbd42 added the suppression in the first place.

Proven by execution rather than inferred: lint of the HEAD file with object_length_linter reported no lints; lint of the reformatted file reported the name at line 118. Re-anchored as a block-scoped nolint start/end pair, which air leaves alone (air-format now Passed and is idempotent).

Had the reformat been committed as-is, the suppression would have been lost invisibly -- no local gate stage would have complained.

### air.toml vs .lintr consistency check

The issue asked. They already agree: air.toml sets line-width = 80 and .lintr sets line_length_linter(80), with matching data-raw exclusions, and air.toml comments say so explicitly. The 89-char line is not a width disagreement -- air will exceed its own line-width when collapsing a single string argument it cannot break. So the trap is narrower than "formatter can outvote the linter": it only bites on unsplittable literals.

### Done criteria

- air-format, end-of-file-fixer and trailing-whitespace all Passed and idempotent over the whole tree
- verify chain docs/registry/lint/check/coverage green
- coverage 100.00000% (unchanged, the hard bar)
- R CMD check 0 errors / 0 warnings / 1 NOTE, the pre-existing suspension-404 one

Not pushed: the account suspension makes push and PR unrunnable, so this is a local commit.

## SITE-cphsnvut: Explore hosting sitemapr as a public web API + landing page

**Status:** todo

### Description

Future idea — revisit later. Expose sitemapr's parse/validate functionality via an online API with a simple landing page, so non-R users can submit a sitemap URL and get the tidy output back.

### Proposed architecture
```
Browser
  -> Cloudflare Pages (static landing page + Turnstile widget)
  -> Pages Function / Worker: (1) verify Turnstile token via siteverify, (2) proxy to backend if valid
  -> Plumber API on Cloud Run (scale-to-zero): fetch + parse sitemap -> JSON
```

### Front end
- Host static landing page (URL input field) on **Cloudflare Pages** (free, unlimited static requests).
- **Cloudflare Turnstile** for bot protection. Note: the client widget only issues a token; it MUST be verified server-side against challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify.
- Do the Turnstile verification + proxy in a **Pages Function / Worker** (same project). Benefits: backend URL stays hidden, no CORS, Turnstile secret never reaches the browser, single free vendor.

### Backend
- Wrap the R logic in a **Plumber** API, containerize on `rocker/r-ver`, deploy to **Google Cloud Run** (scale-to-zero; 2M free req/month). Fly.io/Render/Posit Connect Cloud are alternatives.
- Lock the backend to accept only requests from the Worker (shared-secret header / authenticated origin pull) so it can't be hit directly as an SSRF proxy.

### Guardrails (mandatory for a public fetch-on-behalf service)
- Audit existing `R/ssrf.R` before going live: block private/link-local/loopback ranges, re-check after DNS resolution (rebinding), cap redirects, enforce timeouts.
- Resource caps: max sitemap size, max index fan-out / recursion depth, max child fetches per request, per-request wall-clock timeout.
- Turnstile stops bots, not a determined human submitting a malicious URL — the in-app caps are the real safe; Turnstile is the front-door lock.

### Cost
- CF Pages: free. Workers: free up to 100k req/day. Turnstile: free, unlimited.
- Cloud Run: $0 at low traffic, pennies/1k beyond; egress bandwidth is the line item most likely to surprise.
- Genuinely $0 at demo/low volume. Cold-start tax on scale-to-zero; min-instances=1 (~few $/mo) keeps it warm.

### Next steps when picked up
- Audit `R/ssrf.R` for public-facing adequacy (do this first).
- Scaffold: index.html + Turnstile widget, functions/api/parse.js (verify + proxy), Plumber wrapper + Dockerfile.

## SITE-ctkdkuna: sniff_is_tar() crashes with a bare base R error on NUL-interleaved bytes

**Status:** done

### Description

### Defect

`sniff_is_tar()` (R/sniff.R:64) reads the POSIX tar magic with `rawToChar(bytes[258:262])`. `rawToChar()` raises `embedded nul in string` whenever a NUL byte is followed by a non-NUL byte inside the vector, so any source at least 262 bytes long whose 258-262 window looks like NUL-then-non-NUL makes the SNIFFER ITSELF raise an uncaught base R `simpleError`.

The sniffer is the first thing every entry point calls, so the error escapes the public API:

```r
b <- raw(300L); b[258:262] <- as.raw(c(0, 97, 0, 97, 0))
tf <- tempfile(); writeBin(b, tf)
sniff_format(b)      #> Error: embedded nul in string: '\0a\0a'
validate_sitemap(tf) #> Error: embedded nul in string: '\0a\0a'
read_sitemap(tf)     #> Error: embedded nul in string: '\0a\0a'
audit_sitemap(tf)    #> returns (catches per-source failures) -- ASYMMETRY
```

Verified 2026-07-29 at e35fc57. All-NUL and trailing-NUL windows are fine; only the interleaved pattern throws, which is why 300 zero bytes classifies as "binary" and the bug went unseen.

### Why it matters

1. It violates the errors-vs-findings contract (architecture.md SS3) and the corpus test's own stated invariant #1: 'A bare simpleError is a bug.'
2. It makes the "binary" classification unreachable for exactly the inputs it exists to name. `sniff_is_text()` already treats a single NUL as binary outright -- but `sniff_is_tar()` runs first and crashes before it is consulted.
3. It is reachable from an ordinary URL fetch, not just a local file: any server returning a PDF, an image, or another binary body at a sitemap URL can trip it. NUL bytes interleaved with ASCII are the normal shape of both UTF-16 text and many binary container formats.
4. `audit_sitemap()` survives where `validate_sitemap()` dies, so the three entry points disagree about the same bytes.

### How it was found

Probing a genuine UTF-16LE encoded sitemap while wiring the encoding facts (SITE-vepzywnc). The corpus fixture encoding/utf16-le-bom.xml does NOT catch this: it is a mislabeled fixture (UTF-16 BOM followed by plain ASCII), so it never produces the interleaved window and fails later at the XML parse instead.

### Fix sketch

Compare the magic on the RAW BYTES rather than routing through `rawToChar()` -- e.g. `all(bytes[258:262] == charToRaw("ustar"))`, matching `sniff_starts_with()`'s existing byte-comparison idiom. No decoding is needed to test five ASCII bytes.

### Done

- `sniff_format()` classifies NUL-interleaved bytes as "binary" instead of raising.
- `validate_sitemap()` / `read_sitemap()` return (or raise a CLASSED sitemapr_* condition) for such a source; all three entry points agree.
- A corpus fixture with a genuine interleaved-NUL window locks it in -- the existing utf16-le-bom.xml does not reach the code path.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-29 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

FIXED — 0fea549.

sniff_is_tar() now compares the five magic bytes RAW: all(bytes[258:262] == charToRaw('ustar')), matching sniff_starts_with()'s existing byte-comparison idiom. No decoding is involved, so there is nothing left to raise. A six-line comment at the function records why the string form must not come back.

Repro confirmed at e35fc57 before the change, all four entry points:
  sniff_format(b)      -> Error: embedded nul in string: '\\0a\\0a'   (simpleError)
  validate_sitemap(tf) -> same bare simpleError
  read_sitemap(tf)     -> same bare simpleError
  audit_sitemap(tf)    -> returned a sitemap_audit  (the asymmetry)

After 0fea549 the same bytes behave byte-for-byte like any other binary source:
  sniff_format         -> 'binary'
  validate_sitemap     -> sitemapr_xml_parse_error   (CLASSED)
  read_sitemap         -> sitemapr_unsupported_format (CLASSED)
  audit_sitemap        -> sitemap_audit

Checked against a plain 300-zero-byte file: identical outcome from every entry point, asserted as a test rather than eyeballed. The residual difference between validate_sitemap() and read_sitemap() (which classed condition each raises for a binary source) is PRE-EXISTING and applies to all binary input, not just this window — out of scope here, flagged in case it matters later.

Match tightness verified in both directions: 'ustaX' at offset 257 is NOT tar, and a genuine ustar header still is, so the raw compare did not loosen anything.

Tests: 4 new in test-sniff.R (interleaved, plus a table over all-NUL / trailing-NUL / leading-NUL / high-byte windows, plus the tar-still-matches assertion) and 3 in test-validate-sitemap.R covering entry-point agreement.

DEVIATION from the issue's third Done criterion, deliberately: no corpus fixture was added. test-corpus-fixtures.R states that fixtures/corpus/ is byte-identical to the sibling port's fixtures/, and the sibling ships the same file set, so adding a binary fixture on sitemapr's side alone would diverge the shared corpus — the same reasoning applied on SITE-lcmvzpel. The lock-in lives in test-validate-sitemap.R instead. If the shared corpus should gain a binary/ family, that belongs to SITE-ppojfsed.

Gates at 0fea549: full suite 0 failures, lint clean, coverage 100.00%, check-docs + check-findings-registry pass, corpus golden unchanged, pre-commit incl. air format clean.

SECOND INSTANCE of the same defect class found while auditing the other rawToChar() call sites — filing separately, do NOT consider it covered by this fix: R/robots.R:110 (discover_robots_sitemaps) calls rawToChar(body) on a fetched robots.txt body with no NUL guard, and the surrounding tryCatch wraps only the FETCH. A server returning a binary body at /robots.txt raises the same bare simpleError straight out of the public sitemap_tree(). Verified against a mocked 200 with a ZIP-magic body. The other two sites are clean: R/parse-archive.R:73 truncates at the first NUL before decoding, and R/sniff.R:112 decodes only bytes already filtered to 0x09-0x7E.

## SITE-dcbsvpjf: Index child <loc> gets no protocol rules; duplicate children dropped silently

**Status:** done | **Parent:** nlptpmdqqvmldzbdrfwhwlceepjoksne

### Description

### Claim

Two gaps in how sitemap-index child `<loc>` values are validated.

**(a) No per-`<loc>` protocol rules run on index rows.** `validate_protocol()` is reportedly never called on index rows — `R/validate-sitemap.R:430+` branches to expansion, and `index_protocol_parts()` (`:544`) runs on leaf rows only. So a child sitemap URL gets no length, fragment, userinfo, escaping, or scheme checks. `sitemap-validator` applies its full `<loc>` rule set to `doc.indexEntries` (`src/lib/services/protocol/xml-protocol.ts:124-129`).

**(b) Duplicate child `<loc>` values are dropped silently.** `dedup_and_cap_children()` (`R/index-expansion.R:233-237`) removes duplicates with no finding. `sitemap-validator` branches on root element in `validateCounts` (`src/lib/services/protocol/counts.ts:44-48`) and emits `PROTOCOL_DUPLICATE_LOC` / `PROTOCOL_URL_EQUIVALENT` for index children too.

### Step 1 — Verify before coding (REQUIRED)

1. Build an index whose child `<loc>` has a fragment and one that is 3,000 characters. Confirm no protocol findings fire on either.
2. Build an index listing the same child twice; confirm dedup happens with no finding.
3. Check whether `INDEX_CHILD_OUT_OF_SCOPE` (`R/index-expansion.R:132-146`) is the only rule reaching index rows — note it returns early when `ruleset` is `NULL`, so the **baseline emits nothing at all** on that path. Confirm whether that early return is intended for baseline or is itself a defect. Record the answer; it may deserve its own issue.

### Why it matters

A sitemap index is a sitemap document. Its `<loc>` values are subject to the same protocol constraints, and a duplicate child is a real authoring error worth reporting rather than silently repairing.

### Approach

Run the existing `<loc>` rule set over index rows, and emit duplicate findings before dedup rather than instead of it. Reuse the existing codes — do not mint new ones. Watch that the subject-ref scheme distinguishes index rows from urlset rows.

### Files

- `R/validate-sitemap.R` — index branch
- `R/protocol-validate.R`
- `R/index-expansion.R` — `dedup_and_cap_children()`

### Done

Index child `<loc>` values get the same protocol rules as page `<loc>` values; duplicate children emit a finding before being deduped; the baseline-vs-ruleset question from step 1.3 is recorded.


### Comments

#### 2026-07-29 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

### Step 1 verification — claim (a) PARTLY reproduces, claim (b) FULLY reproduces

Repro run on the **URL path** (mocked index + 3 distinct children), not just a
local file — the local path returns before `expand_index()` and would have
confirmed the conclusion for the wrong reason. Guard against a false green:
each child served a urlset with one non-absolute page loc, so 3x
PROTOCOL_URL_NOT_ABSOLUTE proves rows really flowed through the protocol layer.

#### (b) Duplicate children — reproduces exactly as claimed
Index listing `dup.xml` twice: fetched **once**, **no finding emitted**.
`dedup_and_cap_children()` (R/index-expansion.R:233-237) repairs silently.
Sibling emits PROTOCOL_DUPLICATE_LOC / PROTOCOL_URL_EQUIVALENT for index
children too (counts.ts:38-48 branches on `doc.rootElement`). Confirmed in
source.

#### (a) Protocol rules on index `<loc>` — the claim OVERSTATES the gap
**Length is already covered**, not by the protocol layer but by
`inst/schemas/siteindex.xsd` (`maxLength 2048`) -> SCHEMA_INVALID. Boundary
probed exactly: 2047 clean, 2048 clean, 2049 -> SCHEMA_INVALID. So a 3,000-char
child IS reported today, just under a different code/layer than the sibling.

Genuinely missing on index rows (all confirmed silent):
- PROTOCOL_URL_FRAGMENT   (`...#section` -> nothing)
- PROTOCOL_URL_USERINFO   (`https://u:p@example.com/c.xml` -> nothing)
- escaping rules          (unescaped `&`/space -> nothing)
- scheme rules            (`http://` child -> nothing)

Sibling applies the same three checks to `doc.indexEntries` as to `urlEntries`
(xml-protocol.ts:124-129: checkLocEscaping / checkLocScheme / checkLocUrlRules).

#### 1.3 — the baseline early return is INTENDED, not a defect. No new issue.
`INDEX_CHILD_OUT_OF_SCOPE` is **not** the only rule reaching index rows:
`validate_index_lastmod()` (cdff4d0) also does, and the XSD covers loc bounds.
Its `ruleset = NULL` early return is deliberate and documented in-place —
sitemap-spec §12.2b index-child scope is an *engine interpretation*, not RFC
baseline, and the early return keeps the baseline path byte-identical. Verified
live: cross-site child emits nothing on baseline, INDEX_CHILD_OUT_OF_SCOPE
under both `google` and `bing` overlays. Working as designed.

#### Consequence for the fix
Scope narrows to fragment/userinfo/escaping/scheme + duplicates; length needs
nothing. These are document-local facts, so they belong **before** the
`is.na(src$final_url)` expansion gate in `validate_index_parts()` — same
placement `validate_index_lastmod()` already uses — so a local index file gets
them too. Reusing `#index-child:<loc>` refs per that precedent; the
`#index-child:` vs sibling `sitemap#index-entry:<n>` divergence stays a
SITE-ppojfsed contract decision, not something to settle here.

#### 2026-07-29 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

### Done — 319f755

`validate_index_locs()` (R/protocol-validate.R) reuses `validate_loc_urls()`
wholesale rather than restating a second rule set for index rows. Wired into
`validate_index_parts()` (R/validate-sitemap.R) next to `validate_index_lastmod()`.

Two deliberate departures from the urlset call, both per the Approach note:
- `sitemap_url = NA` makes `loc_out_of_scope()` inert **by construction**
  (`loc_scope_self()` yields NA authority). Index-child scope is the separate
  §12.2b axis owned by `index_child_scope_findings()`; the two never collapse.
  Test pins that PROTOCOL_URL_OUT_OF_SCOPE cannot appear on an index child.
- Refs re-anchor onto `#index-child:<url>` via a total position lookup
  (`index_child_refs()`), not by parsing the ref string, so it cannot drift
  from how `protocol_url_finding()` composes one.

Runs **before** the expansion gate (local index files covered) and on the

## SITE-dqbbbkja: E.4: hreflang reconciliation (PAGE_HREFLANG_MISMATCH)

**Status:** done | **Parent:** ihycidflmgtcvnctecfqldgdulicucex

### Description

### E.4: hreflang reconciliation (PAGE_HREFLANG_MISMATCH)

Governing: `docs/design/layer-e-page-inspection.md` §4, §5.3, §0.3, §0.7.

**A reconciliation/consistency check, not a presence check.** Methods are officially equivalent → missing on-page hreflang when the sitemap carries it is **not** a defect.

#### Facts (Contract B, §4)
Page head `<link rel=alternate>` `(hreflang, href)` set + self-reference presence; extraction status.

#### Predicate (§5.3, safe under sampling)
Emit `PAGE_HREFLANG_MISMATCH` **only when** page hreflang status = `observed` **and** the two **non-empty** sets disagree under ADR-005 identity (case-insensitive BCP-47 tag, canonical-key `href`; relatives resolved against base/`<base>`). An **empty page set vs a populated sitemap set is NOT a mismatch** (excused). `unknown`/`absent` → softened by the unrendered-snapshot caveat, never a verdict.

#### Do NOT reuse the cross-page graph on a sample
`build_hreflang_graph()` (`R/hreflang-graph.R`) builds a **complete** graph; over a sample it is incomplete → false "no return tag". Cross-page reciprocity needs full coverage; out of E.4 scope.

#### Per-engine table (§0.3, resolve suppress-vs-diagnostic)
| Ruleset | verdict | provenance |
|---|---|---|
| Google | consistency diagnostic (equivalence `documented`; conflict-severity `inferred`) | diagnostic |
| Bing | diagnostic only | `documentation_gap` |
| Yandex | sitemap hreflang **discontinued** → page authoritative. **Decision: suppress the sitemap-vs-page mismatch finding under the Yandex ruleset** (a sitemap signal Yandex ignores is not Yandex-actionable); keep it purely diagnostic if surfaced at all. | `documented` |
| **sitemaps.org (baseline)** | base defines no hreflang (`xhtml:link` is a Google extension) → `not_applicable`, **suppressed** | `documented` |

Facts ride per-finding `context` / `evidence$excerpt` per §0.7.

#### Depends on
E.1f, Layer-F assembler (context merge), fold-doc (hreflang interpretation table).

### Comments

## SITE-dsdkjvyw: page_link_header_canonicals() misses a multi-token rel and false-matches a canonical-prefixed one

**Status:** done | **Parent:** nlptpmdqqvmldzbdrfwhwlceepjoksne

### Description

### Claim — verified by execution, not by reading

`page_link_header_canonicals()` (`R/page-canonical.R:80`) selects link-values with:

```r
grepl('rel\\s*=\\s*"?canonical"?', params, ignore.case = TRUE)
```

Ran that predicate directly in R against the branch's own source:

| params | result | correct | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `; rel="canonical"` | TRUE | TRUE | ok |
| `; rel=canonical` | TRUE | TRUE | ok (bare) |
| `; rel="CANONICAL"` | TRUE | TRUE | ok (case) |
| `; rel="canonical alternate"` | TRUE | TRUE | ok |
| `; rel="alternate canonical"` | **FALSE** | TRUE | **miss** |
| `; rel="canonical-ish"` | **TRUE** | FALSE | **false match** |
| `; rel="not-canonical"` | FALSE | FALSE | ok |

Two defects:

1. **Multi-token `rel` only matches when `canonical` comes first.** RFC 8288 §3.3 defines `rel` as a space-separated list of relation types, order-insignificant. `rel="alternate canonical"` is a valid canonical declaration and is silently dropped — a **false `PAGE_CANONICAL_MISSING`** on a page that declares one, or a missed mismatch.
2. **Any relation type prefixed with `canonical` matches.** The trailing `"?` is optional and nothing anchors the token's end, so `rel="canonical-ish"` is read as a canonical declaration — a canonical target invented from an unrelated link.

### What is NOT broken

The segment split `strsplit(toString(values), ",(?=\\s*<)", perl = TRUE)` is sound. Verified it does not tear an entry on a comma inside the target URI (`<https://e.com/a,b>`) or inside a quoted parameter value (`title="one, two"`) — the `(?=\\s*<)` lookahead handles both. No change needed there.

### Step 1 — Verify before coding (REQUIRED)

The predicate results above are reproduced; re-run them through `page_link_header_canonicals()` end-to-end and confirm the two cases surface as a missing/invented canonical in `page_canonical_extract()` before changing the matcher.

### Fix shape

Parse `rel` as a token list rather than substring-matching it: unquote the value, split on whitespace, lowercase, and test set membership. That fixes both defects at once — order stops mattering and `canonical-ish` stops matching.

### Cross-port note

sitemap-validator's equivalent (`src/lib/services/inspection/link-header.ts`, SMV-jyhjaqno) handles both cases; they are pinned there by tests in commit `66d998f` so the two ports cannot drift while this is open. See SITE-hiacsgdb — hreflang needs the same header parsing, so a single shared corrected link-value parser serving both producers is the better shape than fixing this regex in place.

No finding code changes.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-29 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

VERIFIED then FIXED at 3f72c0e (local only -- GitHub account still suspended, gh api user -> 403).

Step 1 reproduced BOTH defects end to end through page_canonical_findings(), not just the predicate:
- rel="alternate canonical" -> header canonicals character(0), status `absent`, emitted PAGE_CANONICAL_MISSING. A false missing on a page that declares a canonical.
- rel="canonical-ish" -> header canonicals "https://example.com/unrelated", status `observed`, emitted PAGE_CANONICAL_MISMATCH naming a URL the page never nominated.
- Control (rel="canonical" agreeing with the loc) -> no finding, so the producer was otherwise sound.

The issue's fix shape was right, and its cross-port note about a SHARED parser was the better call, so that is what shipped: new R/page-link-header.R, consumed by both page-canonical.R and page-hreflang.R (SITE-hiacsgdb, next commit). page_link_header_canonicals() is now 5 lines over it.

The parser handles the RFC 8288 shapes a substring test cannot see, each pinned by a test: parameters split on semicolons OUTSIDE a quoted value (title="a; b"), quoted-pairs unescaped, repeated parameters kept in order (3.4 hreflang), only the FIRST rel honored (3.3), names and rel tokens case-insensitive, valueless parameters, and a link-value with no parameters at all.

ONE GOTCHA WORTH CARRYING FORWARD: the parameter split had to be PCRE. The same alternation under TRE (R's default) returns a SINGLE run spanning the separators -- on '; rel="alternate"; hreflang="de"' TRE matched 31 characters where PCRE correctly yields three params. Both regexes were prototyped against a case table before either went into the package. This is the inverse of SITE-hwemiqne's lesson (drop perl for speed on the hot path): correct here, and this is a per-inspected-page parse, not a per-line one.

The issue also asserted the comma segmentation was sound -- confirmed, unchanged, and now pinned by a test (a comma inside the target reference and inside a quoted parameter value).

Gates: suite 0 failures, lint clean, coverage 100.00%, docs + registry + R CMD check (1 NOTE, the pre-existing URL-suspension one) all pass.




## SITE-dtohylpx: DESCRIPTION declares R (>= 4.0.0) but no CI job ever tests below oldrel-1

**Status:** done

### Description

DESCRIPTION line 'Depends: R (>= 4.0.0)' is an untested claim.

Verified state of CI:
- verify.yml (the pre-push/CI gate) pins no r-version at all -- four setup-r@v2 steps, none with r-version -- so every gate job runs 'release'.
- full-check.yml is the only matrixed workflow: macos release, ubuntu devel, ubuntu release, ubuntu oldrel-1.

oldrel-1 is the oldest R the package is ever built against, which is far above 4.0.0. Nothing would catch a 4.0-incompatible construct until a user on old R hits it, and CRAN takes the declared floor at face value.

Two defensible resolutions -- pick one, do not do both:
1. Raise the floor to what is actually tested (oldrel-1 at time of release) and note it in NEWS.md. Cheap, honest, narrows the audience.
2. Keep 4.0.0 and add an ubuntu R 4.0 job to full-check.yml so the floor is exercised. Costs a runner and may need dependency pinning, since the rurl/pslr chain may not build there.

Acceptance criteria:
- The DESCRIPTION floor equals the oldest R version some CI job builds against.
- The decision and its reason are recorded (NEWS.md entry or a short docs/decisions ADR).

Found during the /tini instruction-file audit on 2026-08-06.

### Comments

#### 2026-08-07 — bartek@turczynski.pl

Resolved by evidence, not by preference: the floor is false, not merely untested.

httr2 is a hard Import (DESCRIPTION: httr2 (>= 1.1.1)) and declares Depends: R (>= 4.1). testthat (>= 3.3.2) and robotstxtr 0.2.0 also require R (>= 4.1.0). So sitemapr cannot be installed on R 4.0 at all -- dependency resolution fails before any of our code runs. 'Depends: R (>= 4.0.0)' has never been true.

Also checked our own sources for post-4.0 syntax: no native pipe (|>), no backslash-lambda. The single grep hit in R/page-link-header.R:93 is a regex escape. So the package's own code is 4.0-clean; it is purely the dependency chain that sets the floor.

This collapses the two options in the description. Option 1 (raise the floor) is correct and option 2 (add an R 4.0 runner) is impossible -- that job could never install deps. Raising to 4.1.0 is a correction, not a narrowing: the 4.0.x audience never existed.

Note R CMD check --as-cran does not catch this; it does not cross-check declared Depends against dependency floors.

#### 2026-08-07 — bartek@turczynski.pl

Done in d7fb10c, merged to main via GitLab MR !1. DESCRIPTION now declares R (>= 4.1) with a NEWS.md 'Requirements' entry recording why. Full verify gate passed on the branch: docs, registry, lint, R CMD check (222s), Status 1 NOTE (the pre-existing URL-404 set from the GitHub suspension, unchanged).

Chose option 1 from the description; option 2 was impossible, since an R 4.0 CI job could never install httr2.

### Fix

One standalone commit that runs `air format` over just these five files and changes nothing else, so the churn is isolated, reviewable, and never contaminates a behavior diff again.

### Notes

- Purely mechanical: no behavior change, so the full suite must be byte-for-byte green before and after.
- Do it BETWEEN feature slices, never inside one -- the whole point is that the diff contains nothing but formatting.
- Worth re-deriving the file list at the time rather than trusting this one: air's output can shift with a version bump.

### Done

`air format R/` produces no diff; a subsequent behavior change to any of the five files yields a diff containing only that change.

    local air on PATH:                 0.10.0  (/opt/homebrew/bin/air)
    .pre-commit-config.yaml pins:      air-pre-commit rev 0.8.2

    R/decompression-validate.R    3 +-
    R/discovery.R                 9 ++-

Do NOT run 'air format' by hand. Just edit and commit; the pre-commit hook formats with the pinned version. Both commits this session (2e2464c, dff1c85) went through cleanly that way - dff1c85's hook reformatted only the newly added code, with zero unrelated churn.

1. The version-mismatch root cause in the 2026-07-29 comment no longer reproduces. Local air is still 0.10.0 and .pre-commit-config.yaml still pins 0.8.2, but they no longer disagree on this tree: I ran the pinned hook over all files, saved the patch, reverted, ran local air format, and diffed the two patches. Byte-identical, 135 lines each. So there is no rewrite war and no reason to avoid running air by hand at present. The advice to bump the pinned rev or drop the local binary is therefore not needed to close this -- though the two versions agreeing today is a coincidence of this tree, not a guarantee.

2. The file list was already known to be wrong (five to four); it is now down to three. R/parse-archive.R has joined R/probe.R in being byte-stable -- presumably reformatted by the hook when it was last touched. Only decompression-validate, discovery and url still drifted, and all three sit inside cklgdzwq list.

### What the sweep actually needed beyond formatting

Reformatting alone does not pass the gate, which is why this could not have been a pure mechanical commit as filed:

- test-discovery-engine.R:189 becomes an 89-character line when air collapses an argument list, failing line_length_linter.
- air relocating a trailing # nolint onto its own line silently broke a live object_length_linter suppression in R/decompression-validate.R. Details on cklgdzwq.

The practical rule this issue landed on -- do not run air by hand, just edit and let the hook format -- stays sound as a default habit, but it is not what fixed the drift. The drift needed a deliberate whole-tree pass, because per-commit hooks only ever see staged files and the pre-push gate has not run since the account suspension.

## SITE-eoqgkcij: E.2: canonical extraction + mismatch (PAGE_CANONICAL_*)

**Status:** done | **Parent:** ihycidflmgtcvnctecfqldgdulicucex

### Description

### E.2: canonical extraction + mismatch (PAGE_CANONICAL_*)

Governing: `docs/design/layer-e-page-inspection.md` §4, §5.2, §0.7.

#### Facts (Contract B, §4) — pure extraction
Every canonical signal, tagged `html_link` (`<link rel=canonical>`) or `http_link` (`Link: …; rel="canonical"` header); raw target; relative→resolved absolute (against response base / `<base>`); fragment; **all** occurrences. Extraction status: `observed` / `absent` / `unknown` / `not_applicable`.

#### Interpretation (§5.2)
- Extract from **both** channels (Google honors the `Link` header incl. non-HTML).
- `PAGE_CANONICAL_MISMATCH`: page canonicalizes to a **different** URL than the advertised `loc`.
- `PAGE_CANONICAL_MISSING`: **info**; fires **only on `absent`**, never `unknown`; softened by the unrendered-snapshot caveat.
- **URL identity (ADR-005 canonical key):** scheme/host lowercase, default-port removal, dot-segment + percent normalization, **fragment dropped**. Raw `loc` retained for `subject_ref`/message.
- **Soften:** sitemap inclusion is a **weaker** canonical signal than redirects/`rel=canonical` (Google `documented`) → a mismatch is a consistency diagnostic, not "the sitemap is wrong".

#### Per-engine table (§0.3, complete the cells)
| Ruleset | canonical channels honored | mismatch verdict | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google | html + `Link` (incl. non-HTML) | consistency diagnostic | `documented` |
| Bing | html + `Link` | diagnostic | pin from Bing docs or `documentation_gap` |
| Yandex | html (+`Link`?) | diagnostic | pin or `documentation_gap` |
| **sitemaps.org (baseline)** | canonical is not a sitemaps.org concept | generic consistency diagnostic, **no engine verdict** | `documented` (base defines none) |

Structured facts ride per-finding `context` (engine) / `evidence$excerpt` (baseline) per §0.7.

#### Depends on
E.1f (fetch pass + integration), Layer-F assembler (context merge), fold-doc (per-engine table).

### Comments

#### 2026-07-19 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

E.2 done. New producer R/page-canonical.R: PAGE_CANONICAL_MISMATCH (warning, ADR-005 key, fragment dropped) + PAGE_CANONICAL_MISSING (info, only on , never unknown/non-HTML). Both channels: <link rel=canonical> (rel case-insensitive, resolved vs <base href>/final URL) + Link header. Wired into page_inspection_finalize alongside transport; inspect_pages=FALSE byte-identical. Flipped the 2 PAGE_CANONICAL_* registry rows deferred-v0.2 -> active. +25 tests. Full --as-cran gate green (1 known NOTE). PR #161 -> main e06df07.

## SITE-fbngvttn: findings-contract.md prose contradicts the shipped registry and code

**Status:** done | **Parent:** nlptpmdqqvmldzbdrfwhwlceepjoksne

### Description

### Claim

`docs/findings-contract.md` describes the ADR-009 engine work as unimplemented, but the code disagrees.

The contract prose at `:188, :196, :411, :430` says the engine-specific codes are `status = deferred-ruleset` and that "no implementation emits these fields yet". In `docs/findings-registry.csv`, **zero rows carry `deferred-ruleset`** — the distribution is 72 `active` and 21 `validator-only`, and the three engine codes are `active` with live emitters (slices S6/S7/S8, merged as `0ce094e`, `0187160`, `c3246ec`).

The contract itself says "the CSV wins for code metadata", so the CSV is authoritative — but the prose actively misleads anyone reading the contract to plan a port.

Two smaller documentation gaps from the same review:
- `ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED_SITEMAP_FORMAT` was minted later by S8 and is documented at `:266-271`, but the "two engine-specific codes" sentence at `:408-410` was never updated to three.
- `NEWS.md` reportedly contains **no mention** of `ruleset`, `ADR-009`, or `engine` — the entire per-engine surface is exported and unannounced.

### Step 1 — Verify before coding (REQUIRED)

1. `grep -n "deferred-ruleset" docs/findings-contract.md docs/findings-registry.csv` — confirm the prose/CSV divergence.
2. Confirm the three engine codes have real emitters: trace `PROTOCOL_URL_DECODED_TOO_LONG` (`R/protocol-validate.R:1417-1436`), `PROTOCOL_TAG_DATA_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (`:435-466`), `ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED_SITEMAP_FORMAT` (`R/classification-validate.R:253`) from registry row to emitting call.
3. `grep -in "ruleset\|adr-009\|engine" NEWS.md` — confirm the changelog gap.
4. Check whether ADR-009 §7's "published supported-sibling-version ranges" exist anywhere. If not, that is a real contract obligation unmet, and the sibling needs them to pin compatibility — record it, possibly as its own issue.

### Why it matters

This document is the cross-repo contract. The sibling port is being planned against it right now, and its prose says the feature does not exist. Stale contract prose is more harmful than missing prose.

### Approach

Update the prose to match the shipped state, correct "two" to "three" engine codes, and add NEWS entries for the per-engine surface. Add the supported-sibling-version ranges if step 1.4 confirms they are missing.

### Files

- `docs/findings-contract.md`
- `NEWS.md`

### Done

No contract statement contradicts the registry or the code; the engine-code count is right; NEWS announces the per-engine entry points; the version-range obligation is either met or tracked.

CORRECTION 2 — 'THREE CALL SITES' IS WRONG; THERE ARE TWO. rurl::clean_url is NEVER called by sitemapr. The only three greps for it in R/ are prose: R/discovery.R:82 and R/protocol-validate.R:74 name it as the thing deliberately NOT used, and a cucumber scenario asserts the identity key is not clean_url. The live call sites are rurl::safe_parse_urls (via rurl_parse in R/url.R) and rurl::rurl_cache_config (R/zzz.R:33). The probe still exercises clean_url, which is harmless but not load-bearing — do not treat clean_url drift as a release blocker.

CORRECTION 3 — THE LOCAL BASELINE HAS ALREADY DRIFTED OFF THE PIN. The system R library at /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.6/Resources/library/rurl now holds rurl 2.8.0, NOT the pinned 2.2.1 that earlier comments recorded as installed. Every local devtools::test() / R CMD check run on sitemapr since then has therefore been running against 2.8.0 while DESCRIPTION still pins Remotes @v2.2.1. That is not currently causing failures (see below), but it means 'it passes locally' no longer evidences the pinned configuration. This run sidesteps it by installing into a provenance-asserted scratch library.

CORRECTION 4 — THE 2.8.0 NEWS FLAGS A BREAKING DEPENDENCY CHANGE THAT DOES NOT APPLY. rurl 2.8.0 drops curl from Imports entirely (parsing is now in-tree; NEWS documents a 106,898-input field-by-field equivalence check at zero differences). Flagged breaking only because a transitive dependency disappears. Checked: sitemapr never calls curl:: — the sole hit in R/ is a comment at R/url.R:233, and url_fast_components_vec() (R/url.R:236) is pure regexec, not a curl split, despite the roxygen prose calling it a 'cheap curl component split'. curl is also not in sitemapr's Imports and stays installed regardless via httr2 (curl >= 6.4.0). No DESCRIPTION change needed on this account.

METHOD. rurl c0c8dca exported from the local clone via git archive, R CMD INSTALLed into a fresh scratch library; sitemapr HEAD (main 75dfe7a) exported to a separate scratch copy. The real working trees were never touched and are still clean. Both the suite and the probe assert provenance in-run (stopifnot the resolved rurl path is under scratchpad).

PROBE: BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS THE REWRITE. The same probe.R as the prior two runs (md5 40eedd0db00a0b0da7dfd5351e1475d4, 23 URLs through safe_parse_urls with sitemapr's four pinned dials, plus clean_url and rurl_cache_config).
- vs 2.7.0/096443d: the ONLY differing line is the '## rurl version:' header. Every parse field identical. This is the striking result — the 33 commits rewrote the parse core (R/parse.R, R/parse-state.R, R/parse-phases.R, R/accessors.R, new R/verdicts.R; 1505 insertions in R/) and produced literally zero observable change on sitemapr's call path.
- vs 2.2.1 (THE PIN): still exactly the two known file:-authority rows flipping parse_status error -> ok. No new deltas.
- Adapter schema intact: 10/10 url_adapter_cols, same 8 extras (password, domain, tld, domain_ascii/unicode, tld_ascii/unicode, clean_url). Fast/slow rbind contract holds.
- rurl_cache_config(max_full_parse=) still accepted; zzz.R's tryCatch stays dormant.
- Ran under options(warn=1): zero warnings. The #254 canonical_join dial warning still does not fire here.
- IDN/non-ASCII and obfuscated hosts: zero drift, third run running.

RISKY COMMITS SCREENED. The userinfo/credential cluster (#274 30 libcurl-refused code points, #275 userinfo percent-encode set, #279 stop discarding credentials on the general route, #282 credentials as parity components) was the live risk since sitemapr parses http(s) URLs that can carry userinfo — the probe's https://user:pw@example.com/x row is unchanged, so none of it reaches the mainline. The WHATWG cluster (#264-#273) targets non-special/opaque schemes (mailto:, opaque paths) that sitemapr never parses. #257 (input names no longer leak into safe_parse_urls row names) touches output shape directly and was tested explicitly: named input now yields rownames 1,2,3, so the rbind + integer-order reindex in parse_url_adapter() is strictly safer than before; moot in practice since sitemapr passes unnamed vectors.

SUITE: FULL PASS under 2.8.0. All test files, 0 failures, 0 warnings, 1 skip (the declared-dependencies OSS Index check, OSSINDEX_USER/OSSINDEX_TOKEN unset) — identical to the 2.2.1 baseline. tests/testthat/_snaps is still empty, so no stored snapshot can silently drift.

BOTTOM LINE. sitemapr is compatible with rurl main as of c0c8dca/2.8.0. Three independent probes at three upstream commits (266c6f3, 096443d, c0c8dca) agree exactly, now spanning a full parse-engine rewrite and a dependency removal — the compatibility claim is well-supported and no longer worth re-deriving on every upstream move. The remaining work is purely mechanical (Remotes @v2.2.1 -> @v2.8.0-or-whatever-ships, optionally raise the >= 2.1.0 floor) and is blocked on TWO events now, in this order: (1) the GitHub suspension being lifted, (2) rurl cutting a release tag. Artifacts: <scratchpad>/revdep/ — install.log, test-new.log, probe.R, probe-221.txt, probe-270-096443d.txt, probe-280-c0c8dca.txt, probe-280.warn.
