## SITE-ygammysr: Reduce cyclomatic complexity in R/protocol-validate.R (validate_hreflang/video/loc + 4 more)

**Status:** done | **Parent:** ahiemmjqawfiwbxbihlbayibwqbicbee

### Description

Reduce cyclomatic complexity of the high-complexity validators in `R/protocol-validate.R`. This is the heaviest file in the sweep — it holds 3 of the 5 prioritised top offenders.

### Offenders (cyclocomp, measured 2026-06-29; threshold > 15)

| Function | cc | In parent list? |
|---|---|---|
| `validate_video_element` | 39 | yes |
| `validate_hreflang` | 39 | yes |
| `validate_loc_urls` | 34 | yes |
| `hreflang_roles` | 25 | yes |
| `validate_extensions` | 24 | yes |
| `validate_text_protocol` | 22 | yes |
| `classify_hreflang_token` | 18 | no (parent list was truncated) |

### Decomposition strategy (behaviour + emitted findings unchanged)

Shared shape across these: a function that does N independent things; each `if`/branch/`&&` adds 1 to the count. Move each "thing" into a named helper to push complexity out of the parent.

- **`validate_hreflang` (39)** — outer row-loop with four phases. Extract:
  - `hreflang_link_findings(alts, base, i)` — the per-link inner loop (attrs, token classify, relative-href); returns the findings list plus the `token_norm` / `is_xdefault` / `xdefault_clean` / `any_hreflang` state.
  - `hreflang_duplicate_findings()`, `hreflang_xdefault_dup_findings()`, `hreflang_xdefault_missing_finding()`.
  - Parent shrinks to a thin orchestration loop. Projected well under 15.
- **`validate_video_element` (39)** — six independent field checks (duration, rating, tag-count, description, the enum loop, the rel loop). Extract a `video_range_msg(value, range, fmt, ...)` helper (covers duration + rating, the two near-identical range guards) and small `video_enum_msgs()` / `video_rel_msgs()` helpers. Most of the 39 is repeated `is.na` + range guards.
- **`validate_loc_urls` (34)** — extract `loc_url_findings(...)` (the per-absolute-URL checks: no-host, length, invalid-escape, fragment, userinfo, out-of-scope) and `loc_duplicate_findings(...)` (the identity-key dup pass). Parent keeps the relative-URL pre-pass + orchestration.
- **`validate_extensions` (24)** — the per-row image/video/news fan-out is already delegated; extract the three per-kind blocks into `extension_image_findings()` / `extension_video_findings()` / `extension_news_findings()` so the row-loop just accumulates.
- **`validate_text_protocol` (22)** — per-line loop emitting blank-line / not-absolute / etc. findings; extract a `text_line_finding(line, n, base)` returning 0/1 findings per line.
- **`classify_hreflang_token` (18)** — already well-factored (delegates to `hreflang_roles` / `hreflang_case_ok`); the count is the precedence cascade. Lower-value; trim only if it falls out naturally.

### Caveat — `hreflang_roles` (25)
Inherently branchy: positional subtag rules (`n == 1/2/3`, alpha2/alpha4 shape tests). Forcing it under 15 likely needs a lookup table that obscures the spec mapping. Recommend a light touch — accept ~16–18 here if lowering hurts readability. This metric is advisory (does not fail R CMD check).

### Safety net & verification
- Pure refactor; the existing suite is the guard (`tests/testthat/test-protocol-validate.R`, `protocol_validation.feature`; package-wide 1198 pass / 0 fail at sweep baseline). No coverage regression (file is at/near 100%).
- Verify per function:
  `Rscript -e 'library(cyclocomp); e<-parse(file="R/protocol-validate.R"); ...'` — or re-run `cyclocomp_package_dir(".")` and confirm these names drop below 16.

### Done when
Top offenders (`validate_hreflang`, `validate_video_element`, `validate_loc_urls`) under threshold; the rest under or with a documented readability exception (`hreflang_roles`). Tests green, coverage not regressed, `devtools::document()` zero-churn.

### Pin robotstxtr v0.2.0 engine-contract-v1 (release tag + Remotes bump)

Governing: `docs/design/layer-e-page-inspection.md` §0.9. **The concrete blocker for E.1b.**

E.1b names v1 engine-contract APIs (`robots_evaluate_url_v1`, `as_legacy_robots_decisions_v1`) that live in `robotstxtr` **0.2.0** (DESCRIPTION `Version: 0.2.0`), but:

- **no `v0.2.0` tag exists** in robotstxtr — the v1 contract is on HEAD only (post PRs #43–45), not released.

#### Steps
1. **Cross-repo (robotstxtr):** tag/release `v0.2.0` at the engine-contract-v1 commit.
2. **sitemapr:** bump `Suggests: robotstxtr (>= 0.2.0)` and `Remotes: …@v0.2.0`.
3. **Gate on the schema revision** — check `robots_engine_contract_v1()$contract_id` at the seam, so an incompatible robotstxtr fails loudly rather than silently.
4. Consume the **public** capability accessor `robots_engine_contract_v1()$matcher_capability`; `engine_backend_capability_v1()` is internal to robotstxtr — do not reach into it.

#### Blocks
E.1b (SITE-kwkggijf), and transitively E.3.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-19 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Done via PR #164, squash-merged to main at 9f5ef0d. E.1b is now unblocked.

Step 1 (cross-repo): robotstxtr v0.2.0 tagged at 7012ed1 (engine-contract-v1, PRs 43-45). Ran robotstxtr's own verify gate at that commit before tagging: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 benign new-submission NOTE. Annotated tag, pushed, dereference confirmed.

Step 2: DESCRIPTION now Suggests robotstxtr (>= 0.2.0) and Remotes at v0.2.0.

Step 3: gate lives in R/robots-validate.R as robotstxtr_engine_contract(), wired into the seam resolve_robots_ua().

Step 4: capability read via the public robots_engine_contract_v1() matcher_capability, wrapped as robotstxtr_matcher_capability(). The internal engine_backend_capability_v1() is never touched.

IMPORTANT deviation from the issue's step 3, worth knowing for E.1b: gating on contract_id alone is NOT sufficient. A pre-PR-43 robotstxtr advertises the SAME robotstxtr.engine-aware/v1 id while carrying schema 2026-07-17.1 and no matcher_capability field at all. Found this empirically -- the robotstxtr build installed locally was exactly that stale one, so the capability test failed with NULL despite a matching id. An id-only gate would pass that build and silently hand out NULL capability, which is the exact silent failure the gate exists to prevent.

The gate now checks three things: accessor exists, contract_id matches, matcher_capability actually present. The known-good schema 2026-07-18.2 is recorded for the error message but deliberately NOT an equality gate, since additive robotstxtr revisions stay compatible and exact-pinning would break sitemapr on each one.

Failure posture: absent robotstxtr stays a warning + graceful skip (setup fact). Present-but-incompatible aborts with a classed sitemapr_robotstxtr_contract error, because wrong matcher semantics would silently corrupt robots findings.

## SITE-ynxpeikq: F.2 validate_sitemap() entrypoint: read/branch, wire C+D+classification+INDEX, source_meta

**Status:** done | **Parent:** ymzvnlprytjfrnfgfrozeujxsndbsfpd

### Description

**Layer F slice — unit F.2 (the `validate_sitemap()` entrypoint + wiring).** Parent epic: SITE-ymzvnlpr.

The public Layer F deliverable: read a single source, run every finding-producer over it, and hand the parts to the F.1 assembler core. This is the integration point — the only place that holds the raw doc/bytes and can test the parse→validate→assemble flow end to end.

### Read first
- `R/read-sitemap.R` (the parallel read path: `read_sitemap_local`, `read_sitemap_url`, `parse_dispatch` — reuse its fetch/sniff/dispatch logic; do NOT duplicate the network code).
- `R/schema-validate.R` (`validate_schema(doc, subject_ref, ...)`), `R/protocol-validate.R` (`validate_protocol(rows, sitemap_url, subject_ref, byte_size, fetched_at, source_meta, limits)` — note F.0 removed `lastmod_raw`; `validate_text_protocol(text, subject_ref)`), `R/classification-validate.R` (`source_meta()`, `validate_classification`, `validate_encoding`).
- `R/parse-xml.R` (`read_sitemap_xml`, `parse_sitemap_xml`), `R/index-expansion.R` (`expand_index`, the `problems` it records), `R/sniff.R` (`sniff_format`), `R/parse-rows.R` (`project_typed_rows` from F.0 — but Layer D consumes the FAITHFUL rows, so keep the un-projected rows for `validate_protocol`).
- `docs/findings-contract.md` (subject_ref scheme, INDEX_* and UNSUPPORTED_* / classification codes), `docs/sitemap-spec.md` §6 (mode), §8 (index expansion → INDEX_* mapping).

### Signature (PRD §example)
```r
validate_sitemap(x, mode = c("strict", "non-strict"), user_agent = default_user_agent(),
                 limits = fetch_limits(), index_limits = NULL)
```
`mode <- match.arg(mode)` → default `"strict"`. `@export`. Returns the assembled findings tibble from F.1 `assemble_findings(parts, mode)`. Add to NAMESPACE (roxygen `@export`); document with roxygen and run `devtools::document()`.

### Flow
1. **Resolve + read the source bytes** (reuse `read_sitemap`'s machinery): local file or URL fetch (SSRF-guarded). Capture the raw bytes, the sniffed format, the uncompressed `byte_size`, and `fetched_at` from the fetch metadata (`sources` record). Build the document-level `subject_ref` base via `sitemap_subject_ref(final_url)`.
2. **Branch on sniffed format**, building the producer `parts` list:
   - **HTML masquerade** (sniffer says HTML at a sitemap source): `parts = [ validate_classification(source_meta(html_masquerade = TRUE), base) ]`. No schema/protocol.
   - **text**: `parts = [ validate_text_protocol(raw_text, base) ]`. (Text never goes through XML schema/protocol — sitemap-spec.md §7.2.)
   - **XML**: parse with `read_sitemap_xml(bytes)`. Inspect root local-name:
     - root not `urlset`/`sitemapindex` → `source_meta(unsupported_root = <root>)` → `validate_classification(...)`. `validate_schema()` already returns empty for an unsupported root; no protocol rows.
     - `urlset` → `validate_schema(doc, base, ...)` + `validate_protocol(faithful_rows, sitemap_url = final_url, subject_ref = base, byte_size = byte_size, fetched_at = fetched_at, source_meta = NULL)`. Get `faithful_rows` from `parse_sitemap_xml()` (do NOT project to typed — Layer D wants the raw `lastmod`/`priority` columns per ADR-004 / F.0).
     - `sitemapindex` → `validate_schema(doc, base, ...)`; expand via `expand_index()`; map the expansion `problems` to `INDEX_*` findings (see step 3); detect RSS/Atom **feed children** and pass them as `source_meta(feed_children = <urls>)` → `validate_classification(...)` for `UNSUPPORTED_FEED`; run `validate_protocol` over the index's own child rows where applicable.
3. **Index problems → INDEX_* findings.** `expand_index()` records non-fatal traversal events as `problems` (category/severity/subject_ref/message; see `R/problems.R`, `R/index-expansion.R`). Map them to the stable codes in findings-contract.md: `SITEMAP_INDEX_NESTED` (warning), `INDEX_CYCLE_DETECTED`, `INDEX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED`, `INDEX_CHILD_COUNT_EXCEEDED`, all `layer = "index-expansion"`. Build contract-shaped rows (a small mapper, e.g. in this file or `R/findings-assemble.R`).
4. **Encoding signals are out of scope for the active features** (no `ENCODING_*` scenario in the three features being activated). `validate_encoding()` already exists and is unit-tested; leave `source_meta`'s `bom_encoding`/`declared_encoding`/`http_charset` unset (NA) for now and add a `# TODO(layer-f-encoding)` note. Do not invent encoding-signal extraction in this unit.
5. **Errors vs findings.** `validate_sitemap()` turns conditions that the parse API would *raise* into *findings* where the contract says so (unsupported root/format/HTML → classification findings, not a thrown error). A genuine transport/SSRF/timeout failure may still surface as documented in the contract (`FETCH_*` notes) — keep v1 minimal: a hard fetch failure can propagate as the existing classed condition unless a feature scenario requires otherwise (none of the three activated features do).
6. **Assemble**: `assemble_findings(parts, mode)` (F.1).

### Tests (`tests/testthat/test-validate-sitemap.R`, direct unit tests)
Offline only (local fixtures + `httr2::local_mocked_responses` for URL/index cases, following the pattern in `tests/testthat/setup-steps-parse.R`). Cover one case per branch:
- Valid urlset → zero findings.
- urlset with a protocol violation (e.g. duplicate loc) → a `PROTOCOL_DUPLICATE_LOC` row present, full 10-column contract.
- Schema-invalid urlset in strict → `SCHEMA_INVALID` error; in non-strict → same code downgraded to warning (proves F.1 transform is wired).
- Unsupported root → `UNSUPPORTED_ROOT`.
- Text sitemap with a long line → `PROTOCOL_TEXT_URL_TOO_LONG`.
- Determinism: same fixture + mode twice → `expect_identical` (findings-contract.md guarantee).

### Acceptance
- `validate_sitemap()` is exported, documented (man page generated), and returns the 10-column contract for every branch above.
- Layer D receives the FAITHFUL rows (no typed projection on the validation path).
- Verify gate passes.

### Verify gate
```
Rscript -e 'lints <- lintr::lint_package(); if (length(lints)) { print(lints); quit(status = 1) }; rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = "--as-cran", error_on = "warning")'
```

### Dependencies
F.0 (faithful parse) AND F.1 (assembler core). Blocks F.3, F.4, F.5.




## SITE-ysoqjxpm: Stamp which layers a run exercised on the findings tibble

**Status:** done | **Parent:** nlptpmdqqvmldzbdrfwhwlceepjoksne

### Description

Surfaced while implementing SITE-sftfhtlv (the passed-checks table).

### Problem

The report has to INFER which validation layers a run exercised, because the findings tibble carries no run manifest. R/report-checks.R report_layer_ran() reconstructs it from the sources tibble, the presence of URL rows, the page_coverage attribute, and the fired findings themselves. That works, but two cases are unprovable and are therefore reported as "not exercised" when they may well have run clean:

- check_robots = TRUE leaves NO trace when every advertised URL is allowed, so a clean robots run is indistinguishable from a skipped one. Only a robots finding proves the layer ran.
- for a gzip or tar payload the source record keeps the OUTER format, so the inflated documents root is unknown and the schema layer stays unproven even though it ran.

The current behaviour understates, which is the safe direction (never claim a check passed that did not run) — but a user who deliberately enabled robots checking is told the robots checks were not exercised, which is wrong in spirit.

### Proposed fix

Have validate_sitemap() / audit_sitemap() stamp the layers a run actually exercised, e.g. attr(x, "layers_run"), alongside the existing page_coverage and precap_totals attributes. The report reads it when present and falls back to the current inference when absent (an older result, or a hand-built findings tibble, must still render).

Watch-outs:
- attributes are dropped by both [ and tibble::new_tibble(), so the assembler has to re-attach by hand — the same trap precap_totals hit (SITE-tudzmegl).
- sitemapr has TWO validate branches (R/validate-sitemap.R and R/audit-pipeline.R) that mirror the same index/XML path; the stamp has to land in both or the audit path silently keeps understating. The audit parity test is the only net.
- schema v1 is the pinned ten-column public contract, so this must be an attribute, never a column.

### Done

A clean check_robots run reports its robots checks as passed rather than not exercised; a gzip source reports its schema checks honestly; the report still renders correctly for a findings tibble with no stamp.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-29 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

VERIFIED then implemented. Commit 4518726.

### Verification (the epic rule), by execution at 48280c0

Both claims CONFIRMED, one of them narrower than filed.

1. Clean robots run. A one-URL sitemap validated with check_robots = TRUE
against an allow-all mocked robots.txt produced 0 findings, and
report_check_states() reported ROBOTS_DISALLOWED, ROBOTS_INDETERMINATE and
ROBOTS_SITEMAP_DISALLOWED all as not-run - despite the layer having fetched
robots.txt and evaluated the URL. report_layer_ran() hardcoded robots = FALSE.

2. Gzip schema. The SAME document reports schema = TRUE as .xml and schema =
FALSE as .xml.gz (corpus/compressed/valid.xml.gz, 4 URL rows parsed). Confirmed.

### Where the claim was too wide

The issue says "for a gzip OR TAR payload ... the schema layer stays unproven
even though it ran". For tar it does NOT run. There are exactly two
validate_schema() call sites in the package (R/validate-sitemap.R:462 and
R/audit-pipeline.R:459), both on the single-document XML path;
validate_archive_parts() reaches neither - it goes parse_sitemap_archive() ->
validate_protocol() with no schema step. So a .tar.gz reporting schema = FALSE is
HONEST, not an understatement, and recording it would have been a false claim.
Only the gzip leg was a defect. This is now stated in R/report-checks.R and
pinned by a test.

### Implementation

New R/layers-run.R: a run-scoped sink the executing code records into, stamped
as attr(x, "layers_run"). It rides on the resolved source (src$layer_sink) the
same way robots_ua and page_sink already do, so recording a layer needed NO new
function argument anywhere. Recorded at the two authoritative points only:
validate_schema()s call site (root already checked, bytes already inflated) and
a non-NULL robots_ua (append_robots_sitemap_part() is unconditional under one,
so the UA itself proves the layer ran).

report_layer_ran() now unions three independent sources of positive evidence:
the existing inference, the stamp, and the fired findings. Evidence only
accumulates, so the safe direction is preserved.

### Both watch-outs in the issue were real, plus two more I hit

- Attribute, not column: done, and the reason is in the file header.
- Two validate branches: both stamp, each at its own validate_schema() call.
  Verified identical by execution and pinned by a test. Worth noting the audit
  parity tests would NOT have caught a divergence - they all pass
  ignore_attr = TRUE - so the test I added asserts the stamps directly.
- NEW: combine_findings_contracts() filters out zero-row parts BEFORE anything
  else, and returns early when all parts are empty. Either would have discarded
  the stamp of a clean run, which is exactly the run this manifest describes. My
  first wiring had this bug. The union is now taken from the unfiltered parts and
  the early return is stamped too; a test drives validate_sitemaps() over two
  clean sources and asserts the stamp survives a 0-row result.
- NEW: audit_sitemap() has neither check_robots nor inspect_pages, so schema is
  the only layer that branch can record. Not a defect, but it is why the two
  branches stamp different sets on a robots run without diverging.

### Done criteria

- Clean check_robots run reports its robots checks as passed: YES.
- Gzip source reports schema honestly: YES.
- Unstamped tibble still renders: YES (falls back to inference; tested).
- A default call still reports robots as not-run: YES - the load-bearing
  negative, tested, since claiming a check ran when it did not is the failure
  mode this section exists to avoid.

### NEWS

No NEWS entry written, deliberately. NEWS.md never announced the Checks section
(SITE-sftfhtlv) or Recommendations (SITE-babrgssv) either, so a line about
refining the Checks table would cite an unannounced feature. Recorded on
SITE-suzycznt, which already tracks a NEWS pass.

Gate: Rscript tools/verify.R green - docs, registry, lint, check with the single
expected URL-suspension NOTE. Coverage 100.00000%.

## SITE-zarjabyz: ENCODING_BOM_DECLARATION_CONFLICT false-positives on the canonical UTF-16 form

**Status:** done | **Parent:** nlptpmdqqvmldzbdrfwhwlceepjoksne

### Description

### Defect

A UTF-16 XML document declaring `encoding="UTF-16"` and carrying a UTF-16LE or UTF-16BE byte-order mark is reported as an encoding CONFLICT. That combination is not a conflict — it is the canonical conformant form.

XML 1.0 SS4.3.3 requires a UTF-16 entity to begin with a BOM, and the BOM is what fixes the byte order; the declaration names the encoding FAMILY. So `encoding="UTF-16"` + a UTF-16LE BOM is the normal spelling, and `encoding="UTF-16LE"` is the rarer one. sitemapr has it backwards: only the rare spelling passes.

### Verified 2026-07-29 at 0fea549

Four synthesized documents through `validate_sitemap()`:

| declaration | BOM | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `UTF-16` | UTF-16LE | **ENCODING_BOM_DECLARATION_CONFLICT** (wrong) |
| `UTF-16` | UTF-16BE | **ENCODING_BOM_DECLARATION_CONFLICT** (wrong) |
| `UTF-16LE` | UTF-16LE | `<none>` (right) |
| `UTF-8` | none | `<none>` (right) |

Message produced: `Byte-order mark indicates UTF-16LE but the XML declaration says encoding="UTF-16"; resolved to UTF-16LE (BOM wins).` The resolution is correct; the finding should simply not fire.

### Cause

`norm_encoding()` (R/classification-validate.R:105) reduces a label to lowercase alphanumerics only — `"UTF-16"` -> `utf16`, `"UTF-16LE"` -> `utf16le` — and `encoding_conflict()` (:298) is a bare `a != b`. Two labels that name the same encoding at different specificity therefore always disagree.

### Scope

Same shape for UTF-32 (`utf32` vs `utf32le`/`utf32be`), which `text_boms` already recognizes. Worth checking the HTTP-charset arm too: a `charset=UTF-16` header against a UTF-16LE BOM hits `ENCODING_CONFLICT` by the same path.

### Why it matters

Both `ENCODING_*` codes only became reachable in e35fc57 (SITE-vepzywnc). Their very first real-world shape — a genuine UTF-16 sitemap — is a false positive, so the codes would land noisy on release. It is also the code the corpus golden pins for `encoding/bom-conflict.xml`, so a fix must be checked against that line rather than assumed inert.

### Approach

Make the comparison family-aware rather than string-equal: a BOM-derived label and a declaration that name the same family at different byte-order specificity are COMPATIBLE, not conflicting. `UTF-16` vs `UTF-16BE` with an LE BOM is still a genuine conflict and must keep firing.

Do not widen `norm_encoding()` itself — it feeds the resolution cascade and the message text, both of which should keep quoting the document's own spelling.

### Done

- `encoding="UTF-16"` + either UTF-16 BOM produces no finding; the resolved encoding is unchanged.
- `encoding="UTF-16BE"` + a UTF-16LE BOM still produces ENCODING_BOM_DECLARATION_CONFLICT.
- UTF-32 behaves the same way; the HTTP-charset arm is checked, not assumed.
- The `encoding/bom-conflict.xml` corpus golden line is re-derived and confirmed still correct.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-29 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Fixed in 2e2464c (local; GitHub account still suspended, unpushed).

### Verified first, at e1ffd50

The filed four-row matrix reproduced EXACTLY as written. Both scope items also confirmed rather than assumed:

| decl | BOM | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| UTF-16 | UTF-16LE | CONFLICT | <none> |
| UTF-16 | UTF-16BE | CONFLICT | <none> |
| UTF-16LE | UTF-16LE | <none> | <none> |
| UTF-16BE | UTF-16LE | CONFLICT | CONFLICT |
| UTF-32 | UTF-32LE | CONFLICT | <none> |
| utf-16 (lowercase) | UTF-16LE | CONFLICT | <none> |

HTTP-charset arm, same shape as suspected: charset=UTF-16 against a UTF-16LE BOM fired ENCODING_CONFLICT before, is silent now; charset=UTF-16BE still fires.

Public surface confirmed by running the same file through validate_sitemap() with the old predicate injected: 1 finding -> 0. read_sitemap() still returns 1 row with the correct loc, so the fix removes a finding, not a capability.

### Fix

New encoding_family() splits a normalized label into family + byte-order suffix; encoding_conflict() treats a byte-order-neutral label as COMPATIBLE with either order from its family. Only utf16/utf32 split, so an unrelated label ending in le/be stays its own family (covered by a test).

norm_encoding() left alone as the issue directed - it feeds the resolution cascade and the message text. resolve_encoding() output unchanged: the BOM still wins.

### Done criteria

1. encoding=UTF-16 + either BOM -> no finding, resolution unchanged. YES
2. encoding=UTF-16BE + UTF-16LE BOM still fires. YES
3. UTF-32 same; HTTP-charset arm checked, not assumed. YES
4. encoding/bom-conflict.xml golden re-derived (REGEN_CORPUS_GOLDEN=1), diff EMPTY. It is a UTF-8 BOM against an ISO-8859-1 declaration - different families - so it legitimately still fires. Confirmed, not assumed.

### Gates

Suite 0 failures (one pre-existing skip, test-security.R:19, OSS Index creds). lint_package() clean. Coverage 100.00%. check-docs + check-findings-registry OK; registry unchanged at 93 codes / 72 active - no code minted. air format no churn.

### Deviation

No corpus fixture added. The end-to-end lock-in builds its UTF-16 document in-test instead, per the byte-identical-corpus constraint. Want recorded on SITE-ppojfsed.

## SITE-zfggbgsj: Robots: flag sitemap document blocked by robots.txt (E.5 sibling)

**Status:** done | **Parent:** ihycidflmgtcvnctecfqldgdulicucex

### Description

### New check: is the sitemap document itself blocked by robots.txt? (E.5 sibling)

Governing: `docs/design/layer-e-page-inspection.md` §0.6.

**Gap (verified):** we parse the robots.txt `Sitemap:` directive for **discovery only** and explicitly ignore `Disallow`/`Allow` there (`R/discovery.R:312`); every robots allow/deny code is fed the **listed `<loc>`s** (`R/validate-sitemap.R:649`), never the sitemap document's own URL. So a sitemap advertised at a path its own robots.txt `Disallow`-es goes uncaught.

#### Decision
Add the **document-level analog of E.5**: test whether the sitemap URL(s) being validated are `Disallow`-ed for the engine's token, via the same `robotstxtr` machinery (reusing the E.1b consultable decision), pointed at the sitemap URL instead of the locs.

- **Class:** engine-aware self-contradiction diagnostic (parallel to the §5.4 robots×noindex trap) — "you advertise a sitemap your own robots.txt blocks". Webmaster tools warn on this; exact fetch mechanics vary by engine, so frame as a consistency diagnostic with per-engine provenance.
- **Layer:** `robots` (a sitemap-document check, **not** per-URL page inspection — sibling to E.5, not part of E.1–E.4).

#### Open sub-decision (settle before coding)
Finding code: a **new `ROBOTS_*` code at `source` scope** (e.g. `ROBOTS_SITEMAP_DISALLOWED`) vs. reuse of `ROBOTS_DISALLOWED` with a `source`-scoped subject. Either way it is a **coordinated shared-registry addition** (cross-repo with `sitemap-validator`), never a silent invention.

#### Depends on
E.1b (consultable per-URL robots decision). Non-blocking for E.1–E.4.

## SITE-zgufvkks: SSRF guard is fail-open on malformed IPv6 literals — decide whether to fail closed

**Status:** done

### Description

Cross-repo mirror of robotstxtr ROBO-udnyuuwn. Deferred out of SITE-mhfmtdxa.
Not a known bypass today; a documented posture that currently leans on rurl
rather than on the guard itself.

### What

Every IPv6 rule in `ssrf_classify_ipv6()` now reads the expanded hextets from
`ssrf_ipv6_hextets()`. That expander returns NULL for anything it cannot
resolve to exactly 8 hextets — three-colon literals (`fe80:::1`), a bad
dotted-quad tail (`::ffff:999.1.1.1`), an over-long hextet (`::12345`), more
than one `::` run. When it returns NULL, no rule matches and the classifier
reaches its default: reason NA, i.e. ALLOWED.

Before SITE-mhfmtdxa the link-local regex would incidentally have blocked some
malformed strings (`fe80:::1` matched `^fe[89ab][0-9a-f]?:`). That was an
accident of string matching, not a policy, and it was inconsistent — most
malformed literals already fell through to allow. The current behaviour is at
least uniform.

### Why it is safe today

ADR-003 §1 specifies that the guard runs on parsed host and IP components from
rurl and does not re-parse the host itself. rurl rejects or canonicalizes
malformed IPv6 literals before the guard sees them, so the fail-open path is
unreachable through the real fetch path.

That is exactly the kind of reliance SITE-vovtwvuh set out to remove for the
IPv6 specials: the guard should be correct on its own rather than depending on
what rurl happens to do. This is the same argument applied to malformed input.

### The decision to make

Options, roughly in increasing strictness:

1. Keep fail-open, documented (status quo). Cheapest; correct as long as the
   rurl contract in ADR-003 §1 holds.
2. Fail closed on a literal that contains a colon but does not expand: return
   a new reason code (`malformed-literal`?) so such a host is refused rather
   than allowed. This adds a code to the stable reason-code list, so it is an
   ADR-003 amendment, not just an implementation change. Needs a check that no
   legitimate host shape regresses — the classifier routes on
   `grepl(":", bare)`, so a registered name containing a colon would newly
   be blocked.
3. Fail closed only for literals whose leading hextet already looks like it is
   in a blocked prefix. Narrow, but reintroduces exactly the literal-prefix
   guessing this fix removed. Probably not worth it.

Recommendation is 2 if the cost is low, since a new reason code is cheap and
the guard stops depending on an external package's parse behaviour. Confirm
first that no non-IPv6 host reaches `ssrf_classify_ipv6()`.

### Land together

Mirrors robotstxtr's copy of the same guard. If this changes, both repos change
byte-for-byte, per the parity discipline in SITE-mhfmtdxa / ROBO-pjvypcjk.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-25 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Posture recorded in ADR-003 §1 plus a matching KNOWN POSTURE note in the R/ssrf.R header, merged as b9f50b8 (PR #176); CI green, branch deleted local+remote. Issue stays todo — the note documents the behaviour, it does not decide it.

ADR-003 §1 also now states the invariant that every IPv6 rule matches on the expanded address rather than the literal string. That had lived only in code comments since SITE-vovtwvuh, despite being the property both parity fixes exist to protect.

Mirrored as robotstxtr ROBO-udnyuuwn (5b1514c, robotstxtr PR #61).

#### 2026-07-25 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Decided option 2 (fail closed) and implemented on fix/ssrf-transition-embeddings (PR #178).

Reason code is malformed-address, NOT the malformed-literal this issue floated. ssrfr's vocabulary already reserves malformed-address for exactly this case (ssrf-guard-spec.md §5 line 457, INV-11), and reason codes are a published compatibility surface -- picking a different spelling now would mean renaming a published value when ssrfr absorbs the matcher (SITE-yeozymry).

The argument for fail-closed over documented-status-quo: it is the same argument SITE-vovtwvuh already accepted for the IPv6 specials, applied to malformed input. The guard should be correct on its own rather than leaning on what rurl happens to do.

Bonus the decision paid for: refusing before any rule runs means every IPv6 rule can now assume 8 numeric hextets, which removed three defensive is.null() branches from ssrf_ipv6_special(), ssrf_ipv6_prefix_block(), and ssrf_embedded_reason(). Four tests that pinned the old fail-open property at helper level (passing NULL directly) were rewritten to assert the new property at classifier level.

No reachable behavior change: rurl rejects these literals before the guard sees them, so this is only observable through ssrf_check() directly. That unreachability is the whole point -- it was the reliance being removed.

ADR-003 §1 amended (the old 'Open, revisit later' block replaced by the decision), plus a Negative/trade-off bullet noting the guard is now stricter than the parse layer rather than the other way round.

Mirrored by hand into robotstxtr as ROBO-udnyuuwn.
